     9	# Writing viewof, mutable and import cells in module source
    10	
    11	A module file under `/src` is the compiled `define()` form, not Observable source. Three Observable
    12	constructs expand into more than one variable there, and each must be written out in full. The
    13	robocoop-5 agent got every one of these wrong at least once on 2026-09-27; the failures are quoted
    14	under each.
    15	
    16	## viewof — two variables
    17	
    18	```js
    19	$def("_k1", "viewof knob", ["Inputs"], (Inputs) => Inputs.range([0, 100], {value: 10}));
    20	$def("_k2", "knob", ["Generators", "viewof knob"], (G, v) => G.input(v));
    21	```
    22	
    23	`knob` is the value; other cells list `"knob"` as an input and recompute when the slider moves.
    24	`Generators.input` is what connects the two: it yields the element's `value` on every `input`
    25	event.
    26	
    27	Observed (e6, game-theory prompt): the value cell was written as `(viewof_marketSize) =>
    28	viewof_marketSize`, so `marketSize` was the element, and every payoff came out `NaN`. The fix the
    29	agent chose, `+viewof_marketSize.value`, reads the slider once when the cell first runs and never
    30	again: the model stopped responding to its own inputs. Both compile and both report "computes
    31	with no runtime error", so the apply result does not catch either.
    32	
    33	## mutable — three variables
    34	
    35	```js
    36	$def("_m1", "initial count", [], () => 0);
    37	$def("_m2", "mutable count", ["Mutable", "initial count"], (M, _) => new M(_));
    38	$def("_m3", "count", ["mutable count"], _ => _.generator);
    39	```
    40	
    41	Read `count` to react to it. Assign through `"mutable count"` (`m.value = 5`). Copied from the

    45	
    46	```js
    47	main.define("module @user/other", async () => runtime.module((await import("/@user/other.js?v=4")).default));
    48	main.define("x", ["module @user/other", "@variable"], (_, v) => v.import("x", _));

     7	# Time windows and time zones in data fetched from a web API
     8	
     9	A cell that fetches timestamped rows (a forecast, prices, sensor readings, metrics) and charts them
    10	has two ways to be wrong while every cell computes without error: the window is not the one asked
    11	for, or every point sits at the wrong instant. Neither shows up as an error, and both are hidden
    12	when the page happens to run at midnight or in the API's own time zone.
    13	
    14	## "Next N hours" and "last N days" start at now
    15	
    16	A relative window is rolling: "the next 48 hours" at 15:30 runs from 15:30 today to 15:30 in two
    17	days. API parameters counted in calendar days start at 00:00 of the current day, so they include
    18	the hours already past.
    19	
    20	Measured on Open-Meteo, 2026-09-28 (`api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast?...&hourly=temperature_2m`):
    21	
    22	| parameter | first row | rows |
    23	|---|---|---|
    24	| `forecast_days=2` | 00:00 today | 48, of which the hours before now are in the past |
    25	| `forecast_days=3` | 00:00 today | 72 |
    26	| `forecast_hours=48` | the current hour | 48 |
    27	
    28	In three runs of the robocoop-5 agent on "the next 48 hours" (2026-09-28, mimo-v2.5-pro) it used
    29	`forecast_days=3` once and `forecast_days=2` twice; at 15:30 all three charts began at 00:00, one
    30	with its own "now" marker drawn a third of the way along the axis.
    31	
    32	Either request an hour-based range, or compute the window from the clock and filter **both** ends.
    33	The house form, from `@tomlarkworthy/cw-share-auth` (aws-dashboard.html), sends absolute instants:
    34	
    35	```js
    36	const end = new Date(), start = new Date(end - 3 * 3600 * 1000);
    37	```
    38	
    39	and the filter for data that arrives in whole days:
    40	
    41	```js
    42	rows.filter(r => r.time >= start && r.time <= end)
    43	```
    44	
    45	## A timestamp without an offset is read as the viewer's local time
    46	
    47	`new Date("<DATE>")` is 13:00 in the browser's time zone, whatever zone the API meant.
    48	Open-Meteo returns such strings in the zone named by its `timezone` parameter, `GMT` when it is
    49	absent, so omitting `timezone` and parsing with `new Date(t)` moves every point by the viewer's
    50	UTC offset (two hours in Berlin in summer).
    51	
    52	Ask for a form that carries its own instant, and convert once, in the cell that builds the rows:
    53	
    54	- epoch seconds: Open-Meteo `timeformat=unixtime`, then `new Date(t * 1000)`
    55	- an ISO string with `Z` or `+02:00`: `new Date(t)` is then exact
    56	
    57	`@tomlarkworthy/cw-metrics.cwDashboard` (aws-dashboard.html) normalises both shapes the same way:
    58	
    59	```js
    60	const toDate = (t) => {
    61	  if (t instanceof Date) return t;
    62	  const n = Number(t);
    63	  return new Date(Number.isFinite(n) && n < 1e12 ? n * 1000 : (Number.isFinite(n) ? n : t));
    64	};
    65	```
    66	
    67	## The axis shows the viewer's zone
    68	
    69	Plot draws a time axis in the browser's local zone; `x: {type: "utc"}` draws it in UTC. A reader
    70	asking about a place in another zone needs to know which one they are looking at: label the axis
    71	(`x: {label: "Time (your local time)"}`) or format ticks in the place's zone with
    72	`tickFormat: d => d.toLocaleString("en-GB", {timeZone: "Europe/Berlin", hour: "2-digit", day: "numeric"})`.
    73	
    74	## Check it before finishing
    75	
    76	Inspect the rows cell and compare its first and last `time` with the current time shown in the
    77	environment block: for "next 48 hours" the first is within the current hour and the last about 47
    78	hours later.

    54	## Where to read, from inside the notebook
    55	
    56	The only web access is `fetch()` in `eval_js`, so an endpoint is usable only if it sends
    57	`Access-Control-Allow-Origin`. Measured 2026-09-27 (headless Chromium from this notebook's page, and
    58	`curl -H 'Origin: null'` for the header):
    59	
    60	| need | URL | CORS |
    61	|---|---|---|
    62	| find candidate packages | `https://registry.npmjs.org/-/v1/search?text=<words>&size=10` | yes (Chromium) |
    63	| find candidate repos | `https://api.github.com/search/repositories?q=<words>` (60 requests/hour unauthenticated) | yes |
    64	| versions, `latest` tag | `https://data.jsdelivr.com/v1/packages/npm/<pkg>` | yes |
    65	| file list of a version | `https://data.jsdelivr.com/v1/packages/npm/<pkg>@<ver>?structure=flat` | yes |
    66	| README, type declarations, any shipped file | `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/<pkg>@<ver>/<path>` | yes |
    67	| a single-file ESM build | `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/<pkg>@<ver>/+esm` | yes |
    68	| project doc sites (`docs.abcjs.net`, …) | | **no** header, so `fetch` fails |
    69	| `npmx.dev` JSON | | **no** |

    71	A library's own docs site usually cannot be fetched. What it ships in the package can: `README.md`,
    72	`types/index.d.ts` or `*.d.ts` (the `types`/`typings` field of `package.json` names it), and often
    73	`docs/` or `examples/`. The file list tells you which exist.

    79	const files = await (await fetch(`https://data.jsdelivr.com/v1/packages/npm/abcjs@${ver}?structure=flat`)).json();

     6	
     7	# Keeping user state in the saved notebook file (localStorage does not travel)
     8	
     9	A Lopecode notebook is one HTML file. "It should still be there next time I open the notebook" means
    10	the state is written into that file when the notebook is saved (Save in place, or export), so it
    11	reopens with the file: in another browser, on another machine, or after the file is emailed.
    12	
    13	`localStorage`, `sessionStorage` and IndexedDB are none of these. They belong to one browser profile
    14	and one origin, are not part of the file, and throw on an opaque origin (a `blob:` fork). Use them
    15	only for per-browser settings that must *not* travel with the file: API keys, a model choice, a
    16	panel toggle. The corpus uses them for exactly that (`@tomlarkworthy/local-storage-view`, the
    17	robocoop-5 model picker and key field).
    18	
    19	Observed (run 20260927-2352-w6, todo-list prompt): the agent kept the list in
    20	`localStorage.getItem("todo-list")` and reported that items "persist across page reloads and
    21	notebook reopenings". After an export and a reopen in a fresh browser context, the list was empty.
    22	
    23	## JSON state: `sticky` rewrites the cell's own source
    24	
    25	`@tomlarkworthy/sticky` wraps any view. The second argument is a literal slot; on every `input`
    26	event from the view, sticky writes `JSON.stringify(view.value)` into that slot in the cell's
    27	definition. Saving the notebook saves the source, so the value comes back on reopen.
    28	
    29	From `@tomlarkworthy/codestrates.doc` (lopebooks `tomlarkworthy_codestrates.html`), a whole HTML
    30	document kept this way:
    31	
    32	```js
    33	const <PID> = function _doc(sticky,codestrate,defaultCodestrate) {return (sticky(codestrate({ value: defaultCodestrate }), "<!doctype html>…"))};
    34	```
    35	
    36	Module source for a list, with the import (sticky is fetched from observablehq.com on first write
    37	and embedded in the file from then on):
    38	
    39	```js
    40	const _viewof_todos = function viewof_todos(sticky, todoList){return( sticky(todoList(), []) )};
    41	…
    42	  $def("_viewof_todos", "viewof todos", ["sticky", "todoList"], _viewof_todos);
    43	  $def("_todos", "todos", ["Generators", "viewof todos"], (G, v) => G.input(v));
    44	  main.define("module @tomlarkworthy/sticky", async () => runtime.module((await import("/@tomlarkworthy/sticky.js?v=4")).default));
    45	  main.define("sticky", ["module @tomlarkworthy/sticky", "@variable"], (_, v) => v.import("sticky", _));
    46	```
    47	
    48	The view must follow the Observable view contract, because sticky only talks to it through that.
    49	Sticky restores a saved value by **assigning `el.value` when the cell runs**, so the setter must
    50	re-render. A setter that only stores the value leaves the reopened list blank while the data is in
    51	the source. From `@tomlarkworthy/codestrates.codestratePlace` (lopebooks
    52	`tomlarkworthy_codestrates.html`, used as `sticky(codestratePlace($0))`):
    53	
    54	```js
    55	  Object.defineProperty(root, "value", {
    56	    get: () => state,
    57	    set: (v) => {
    58	      state = { where: v?.where === "webstrate" && v?.url ? "webstrate" : "notebook", url: v?.url || "" };
    59	      render();
    60	    }
    61	  });
    62	  render();
    63	  return root;
    64	```
    65	
    66	- `get` returns the state, JSON-serializable (arrays, objects, strings, numbers).
    67	- `set` replaces the state **and calls `render()`**.
    68	- after each user edit, `el.dispatchEvent(new Event("input", {bubbles: true}))`; sticky writes the
    69	  slot on that event.
    70	
    71	`Inputs.*` widgets already satisfy this: `sticky(Inputs.range([0, 100], {value: 50}), 50)`.
    72	
    73	One `sticky(` call per cell. Binary or large state (images, audio, datasets) goes in a file
    74	attachment instead (`how-file-attachments-work.md`).
    75	
    76	## Tell the user to save
    77	
    78	The state is in the page until the file is saved. After building it, say so: use Save in place (or
    79	export) before closing the tab.
    80	
    81	## Checking it
    82	
    83	`inspect_value` on the cell only shows the live value. Check both halves:
    84	
    85	1. Saving: drive the view (`eval_js`: set `.value`, dispatch `input`), then read `/notebook/<id>.js`;
    86	   the sticky slot must hold the new value.
    87	2. Reopening: set `.value` WITHOUT dispatching (what sticky does at boot) and confirm the element
    88	   now shows the items (`viewof_todos.textContent`).

    13	# Event handlers and buttons in cells: htl.html, not html; a button that acts on another cell's input; a download button; two inputs that update each other; a custom control (pad, canvas); limiting a number box to a range
    14	
    15	A cell that builds a clickable element and passes it a function (`onclick=${() => …}`) must build it
    16	with `htl.html`. The bare `html` built-in in a Lopecode notebook is the legacy stdlib template: it
    17	converts every interpolated value to a string, so the handler never becomes a listener.
    18	
    19	## What `html` does with a function
    20	
    21	Observed (robocoop-5, pomodoro prompt, 2026-09-27): the agent wrote
    22	
    23	```js
    24	const _toggleBtn = function toggleBtn(ru, mru, html){
    25	  return html`<button onclick=${() => { mru.value = !mru.value; }}>${ru ? '⏸ Pause' : '▶ Start'}</button>`;
    26	};
    27	```
    28	
    29	The arrow was stringified into the attribute; the `>` of `=>` ended the tag. The live button had
    30	attributes `onclick="()"` and `==""`, `typeof button.onclick` was `"object"` (null), and its text was
    31	`{ mru.value = !mru.value; }> ▶ Start`. Clicking it did nothing. The write still reported "all 18
    32	cells compute with no runtime error".
    33	
    34	## The form the corpus uses
    35	
    36	`htl.html` binds a function-valued `on…` attribute as an event listener. `@tomlarkworthy/gallery`
    37	`card` (lopebooks/notebooks/@tomlarkworthy_gallery.html) writes a mutable from a button this way:
    38	
    39	```js
    40	htl.html`<button class="card-star" onclick=${(e) => {
    41	  e.stopPropagation();
    42	  const current = new Map($edits.value);
    43	  …
    44	  $edits.value = current;
    45	}}>${featured ? "★" : "☆"}</button>`
    46	```
    47	
    48	`$edits` is that cell's name for its `"mutable edits"` input. The same shape in a module file, for a
    49	start/pause toggle:
    50	
    51	```js
    52	const _toggle = function toggle(htl, running, $running){return(
    53	  htl.html`<button onclick=${() => { $running.value = !running; }}>${running ? "Pause" : "Start"}</button>`
    54	)};
    55	// in define():
    56	$def("_toggle", "toggle", ["htl", "running", "mutable running"], _toggle);
    57	```
    58	
    59	`htl` is a built-in: list it as an input, as with `md` or `Inputs`. `@tomlarkworthy/lopecode-tour`
    60	`ui_prose` (lopecode/notebooks/@tomlarkworthy_lopecode-tour.html) has a smaller example:
    61	`htl.html\`<button onclick=${(e) => {e.target.innerHTML = "thanks"; e.stopPropagation()}}>click me!</button>\``.
    62	
    63	On 2026-09-27 an `on…=${…}` handler appeared inside `htl.html` in 247 notebook files (modules
    64	including `view`, `mermaid-lens`, `svg-lens`, `viewroutine`, `gallery`, `spreadsheet`,
    65	`lopecode-tour`). The bare-`html` form appeared in 16 files across 10 modules (`@endpointservices/login`,
    66	`animation`, `rate-estimation` and others), all written on observablehq.com, where `html` is htl. In
    67	Lopecode those handlers render as text too.
    68	
    69	## A button that acts on another cell's input
    70	
    71	The action runs once per click and reads the other input's value at click time. The cell holding the
    72	button lists the input's `viewof` and reads `.value` inside the click function.
    73	`@tomlarkworthy/editor-5` `up` (in 224 notebook files, e.g. lopebooks/notebooks/@tomlarkworthy_robocoop-5.html)
    74	reads `viewof editedCell` this way:
    75	
    76	```js
    77	const <PID> = function _up(Inputs,moveCell,$0){return(
    78	Inputs.button("⬆", {
    79	  reduce: () => moveCell($0.value, -1)
    80	})
    81	)};
    82	// in define():
    83	$def("<PID>", "viewof up", ["Inputs","moveCell","viewof editedCell"], <PID>);
    84	```
    85	
    86	The same `$0.value` read works inside an `htl.html` `onclick=${…}` function. When other cells show the
    87	result, `reduce` can return it (or a promise of it): the button's value cell then changes once per
    88	click, and cells that list it recompute once per click.
    89	
    90	Four forms that compile, report "all cells compute with no runtime error", and do not work. All four
    91	were written by robocoop-5 for "a text box and a button that summarises it" (20260928-0300-w19):
    92	
    93	- **The action cell lists the text's value cell** (`"inputText"`). It re-runs on every keystroke, so
    94	  the request is sent while the user types, and the button does nothing the text had not already done.
    95	- **A cell body that waits for a click** (`await new Promise(r => btn.addEventListener('click', r, {once: true}))`
    96	  in a `while (true)` loop). The cell's value never settles. In a replay of that module, text was typed,
    97	  the button clicked, and no request was sent.
    98	- **Finding the input through the DOM** (`btn.closest('.observablehq').querySelector('textarea')`,
    99	  `document.querySelector(…)`). Each cell renders into its own element, so the search from the
   100	  button's cell finds nothing; the handler read `''` and every click showed "Please paste some text first".
   101	- **Adding a listener to another cell's element from a cell that re-runs** (`summarizeButton.addEventListener('click', …)`
   102	  in a cell that also lists `model`). Each run adds one more listener and none is removed, so after the
   103	  model changed one click sent two requests, one with the old model.
   104	
   105	- **A click count that gates an action cell** (`viewof save = Inputs.button("Save")`, then a cell that
   106	  lists `save` and the form's value cells, `save > 0 && (() => { …; a.click(); })()`). After the
   107	  first click the count stays above 0, so the cell runs again whenever any listed value changes.
   108	  Observed (robocoop-5, a form with a download button, 20260928-0847-w10): after one click, editing
   109	  one text field twice offered two more downloads with no click.
   110	
   111	`Inputs.button` is the other working form when the button only needs to count clicks or emit a
   112	value; it is a `viewof` and follows the viewof page (`writing-cells-in-module-source.md`).
   113	
   114	## A button that downloads a file
   115	
   116	The cell's value is the button. The file is built and saved inside its click handler, so nothing is
   117	saved until it is clicked. The cell may list the values the file is made from; when they change the
   118	cell returns a new button and saves nothing. `@tomlarkworthy/suminagashi` `_download`
   119	(lopebooks/notebooks/@tomlarkworthy_suminagashi.html) saves a PNG this way. The same shape for a CSV:
   120	
   121	```js
   122	const _saveCsv = function saveCsv(htl, d3, rows){return(
   123	  htl.html`<button onclick=${() => {
   124	    const blob = new Blob([d3.csvFormat(rows)], {type: "text/csv"});
   125	    const link = htl.html`<a download="rows.csv" href=${URL.createObjectURL(blob)}>`;
   126	    link.click();
   127	    setTimeout(() => URL.revokeObjectURL(link.href), 1000);
   128	  }}>Download CSV</button>`
   129	)};
   130	// in define():
   131	$def("_saveCsv", "saveCsv", ["htl", "d3", "rows"], _saveCsv);
   132	```
   133	
   134	An async builder (a zip, a PDF) goes inside the handler: `onclick=${async () => { const blob = await build(rows); … }}`.
   135	The stdlib `DOM.download(blob, name, label)` returns a ready control too
   136	(`@tomlarkworthy/fileattachments` `_download_selected`, lopecode/notebooks/@tomlarkworthy_atlas.html);
   137	its first click builds the file and relabels the button "Download"; a second click saves it
   138	(`download.js` in the stdlib awaits the value before it sets `href`).
   139	
   140	## Listening on an Inputs view; two inputs that update each other
   141	
   142	An `Inputs.*` view (`Inputs.number`, `Inputs.text`, `Inputs.range`, …) is a `<form>` that wraps a
   143	label and the control. It is not the `<input>`. The view has `value` (read and write), and `input`
   144	events from the control bubble up to it. `document.activeElement` is never the view, because focus is
   145	on the `<input>` inside it, and the view has no `valueAsNumber`. The inner element is
   146	`view.querySelector("input")`.
   147	
   148	Observed (robocoop-5, temperature converter, 20260928-0510-w25): the agent guarded each listener with
   149	`document.activeElement === viewof_celsius` and read `viewof_celsius.valueAsNumber`. The guard was
   150	always false, so typing in either box changed nothing. The write reported "all 10 cells compute with
   151	no runtime error", and the agent told the user the converter worked. With the guard changed to
   152	`viewof_celsius.contains(document.activeElement)` and `.valueAsNumber` changed to `.value`, the same
   153	module passed.
   154	
   155	Two controls that show one quantity: keep the quantity in one hidden state cell,
   156	`viewof celsius = Inputs.input(20)`, and bind each control to it. `Inputs.bind(target, source)` copies
   157	`source.value` into the control, and on the control's `input` event writes the value back to the state
   158	and dispatches `input` on it, so the `celsius` value cell and every other bound control update. The
   159	corpus binds a second control to an existing view this way: `@tomlarkworthy/dataflow-templating` `_dtv2j`
   160	(lopecode/notebooks/@tomlarkworthy_atlas.html) is `Inputs.bind(Inputs.range([1, 4], { label: "widgets",
   161	step: 1 }), $0)` on `viewof widgetCount`. `Inputs.bind` copies values unchanged, so a control that
   162	shows a converted value needs a bind with a function each way:
   163	
   164	```js
   165	const _celsius = function celsius(Inputs){return( Inputs.input(20) )};
   166	const _bindVia = function bindVia(){return(
   167	(target, source, to, from, invalidation) => {
   168	  let fromTarget = false;
   169	  const onSource = () => { if (!fromTarget) target.value = to(source.value); };
   170	  const onTarget = () => {
   171	    if (!Number.isFinite(target.value)) return;
   172	    fromTarget = true;
   173	    source.value = from(target.value);
   174	    source.dispatchEvent(new Event("input", {bubbles: true}));
   175	    fromTarget = false;
   176	  };
   177	  onSource();
   178	  target.addEventListener("input", onTarget);
   179	  source.addEventListener("input", onSource);
   180	  invalidation?.then(() => source.removeEventListener("input", onSource));
   181	  return target;
   182	}
   183	)};
   184	const _cBox = function cBox(Inputs, $celsius, invalidation){return(
   185	  Inputs.bind(Inputs.number({label: "Celsius (°C)"}), $celsius, invalidation)
   186	)};
   187	const _fBox = function fBox(Inputs, bindVia, $celsius, invalidation){return(
   188	  bindVia(Inputs.number({label: "Fahrenheit (°F)"}), $celsius,
   189	    c => Math.round((c * 9 / 5 + 32) * 100) / 100, f => (f - 32) * 5 / 9, invalidation)
   190	)};
   191	// in define():
   192	$def("_celsius", "viewof celsius", ["Inputs"], _celsius);
   193	main.variable(observer("celsius")).define("celsius", ["Generators", "viewof celsius"], (G, _) => G.input(_));
   194	$def("_bindVia", "bindVia", [], _bindVia);
   195	$def("_cBox", "cBox", ["Inputs", "viewof celsius", "invalidation"], _cBox);
   196	$def("_fBox", "fBox", ["Inputs", "bindVia", "viewof celsius", "invalidation"], _fBox);
   197	```
   198	
   199	The control cells list `viewof celsius`, not `celsius`, so they are not rebuilt on each keystroke.
   200	Setting `.value` dispatches no event, so writes do not echo. `fromTarget` stops the state's `input`
   201	event from rewriting the box being typed in: without it, typing `98.60` in °F was reformatted to `98.6`
   202	under the cursor (probe `tools/scratch/rc5-sessions/s37-shared-state-bind.mjs`, 2026-09-28). With it,
   203	typing °F=212, °C=-40, °F=98.6 gave `celsius` 100, -40, 37, the other box 100, -40, 37, and the typed
   204	text kept each time.
   205	
   206	A listener cell that writes each box's converted value into the other box's `.value` also passes the
   207	converter eval, and this page recommended it until 2026-09-28. It leaves no single value to depend
   208	on: the `fahrenheit` value cell does not update when °C is typed, because setting `.value` dispatches
   209	nothing (follows from the no-echo behaviour above; not measured separately).
   210	
   211	## A custom control: set `.value`, then dispatch `input`
   212	
   213	A `viewof` cell can return any element: a pad, a canvas, an svg. The runtime reads the element's
   214	`.value` when the element dispatches `input`, so the value has to be set before the event:
   215	
   216	```js
   217	el.addEventListener("pointerdown", () => {
   218	  el.value = el.value + 1;                              // first
   219	  el.dispatchEvent(new Event("input", {bubbles: true})); // then
   220	});
   221	```
   222	
   223	Observed (robocoop-5 pairing, drum pad, 2026-09-28): the agent's pad dispatched `input` and then set
   224	`.value`, so each hit showed the previous hit's value. Every cell computed and the write reported no
   225	error. The user found it by playing the pad. `try_control` now presses a custom control with the
   226	pointer (down, up, click at its centre) when no `value` is given, and names this cause when the
   227	element's `.value` moved but the value cell did not. Probe `tools/scratch/rc5-sessions/s69-try-control-presses-custom-view.mjs`
   228	builds both orders: the lagging pad is flagged, the other reports `hits 0 → 1`.
   229	
   230	`setPointerCapture` inside a synthetic or already-released pointer event throws `NotFoundError`
   231	(seen in the same session, uncaught). Wrap it in `try`, or leave it out for a press that does not drag.
   232	
   233	## Limiting a number box: the range is the first argument
   234	
   235	`Inputs.number([min, max], options)` and `Inputs.range([min, max], options)` take the limits as the
   236	first argument. There is no `min` or `max` option: `Inputs.number({min: 0, max: 500})` ignores both
   237	without an error (`createRange` in `vendor/observable-inputs/src/range.js` destructures `extent:
   238	[min, max]` from the first argument and never reads `options.min`). `Inputs.range({min, max})`
   239	throws `object is not iterable`.
   240	
   241	Typed into the box the way a user does (probe `tools/scratch/rc5-train/20260928-0847/m31/inputs-behaviour.mjs`,
   242	2026-09-28, the Inputs shipped in robocoop-5):
   243	
   244	```
   245	typed   Inputs.number({min: 0, max: 500, value: 100})   Inputs.number([0, 500], {value: 100})
   246	-5      value -5, box valid                             value stays 100, box :invalid
   247	600     value 600, box valid                            value stays 100, box :invalid
   248	""      value unchanged, box :invalid                   value stays 100, box :invalid
   249	250     value 250                                       value 250
   250	```
   251	
   252	With the extent, an out-of-range, empty or non-numeric entry keeps the last good value and
   253	dispatches nothing, so dependent cells do not recompute; the box shows the entry the value does not
   254	have. A cell that should say what is wrong has to read the box itself
   255	(`viewof x.querySelector("input")`) or take `Inputs.text` and parse it.
   256	
   257	Observed (rc5-train m26, 2026-09-28, "make the AQI converter handle bad input"): in 3 of 3 runs the
   258	agent wrote `Inputs.number({ label: "AQI", value: 100, step: 1, min: 0, max: 500 })` and told the
   259	user the box now refuses values outside 0–500. It accepted -5 and 600.
   260	
   261	The corpus form, `@tomlarkworthy/inputs-reference._number_example`
   262	(lopebooks/notebooks/@tomlarkworthy_inputs-reference.html):
   263	
   264	```js
   265	Inputs.number([0, 10000], { label: 'price', value: 99, step: 0.01 })
   266	```
   267	
   268	A one-sided limit is `Inputs.number([0, Infinity], …)`: a non-finite or `null` end is no limit
   269	(`range.js`, `if (max == null || isNaN(max = +max)) max = Infinity`).

     7	# Writing unit tests in a notebook
     8	
     9	A unit test in a Lopecode module is a cell whose name starts with `test_`. It passes when it
    10	returns a defined value and fails when it throws. `@tomlarkworthy/tests`, which is already loaded
    11	in this notebook, finds every `test_*` cell in every module by reflection and reports each one as
    12	passing, failing or pending. There is no suite object to register with and no runner to call.
    13	
    14	## A test cell
    15	
    16	Copied from `@tomlarkworthy/cell-map._test_recovers_this_notebooks_own_cells`
    17	(`lopecode/notebooks/@tomlarkworthy_cell-map.html`), written here in module source:
    18	
    19	```js
    20	const _test_valid_hyphenated = function _test_valid_hyphenated(isValidISBN13){
    21	  const got = isValidISBN13("978-0-306-40615-7");
    22	  if (got !== true) throw Error("978-0-306-40615-7: expected true, got " + got);
    23	  return got;
    24	};
    25	// inside define():
    26	$def("_test_valid_hyphenated", "test_valid_hyphenated", ["isValidISBN13"], _test_valid_hyphenated);
    27	```
    28	
    29	With `expect` (`@tomlarkworthy/robocoop3-training._test_hello`,
    30	`lopebooks/notebooks/@tomlarkworthy_robocoop3-training.html`):
    31	
    32	```js
    33	const _test_rejects_bad_check_digit = function _test_rejects_bad_check_digit(expect, isValidISBN13){
    34	  expect(isValidISBN13("9780306406158")).toBe(false);
    35	  return "rejected";
    36	};
    37	```
    38	
    39	Rules:
    40	
    41	- **Return a defined value.** A cell that asserts and falls off the end is `undefined`, which the
    42	  headless runner (`lope-browser-runner.ts --run-tests`) reports as a timeout, not a pass.
    43	  `expect(...).toBe(...)` itself returns `undefined`, so return something after it.
    44	- **One case per cell** when the user wants to see which cases pass: each `test_*` cell is one row
    45	  in the results. A single cell that loops over a table stops at the first failure and shows one row.
    46	- **The expected value is a literal you worked out independently.** A test that compares the
    47	  function with itself, or with a second copy of the same algorithm, cannot fail.
    48	- **Cover both outcomes.** Include cases that must return `true` and cases that must return `false`
    49	  (or throw). A suite of only valid inputs still passes when the function always returns `true`.
    50	- **Tests live in the module they test**, next to the function, not in a separate `-tests` module.
    51	
    52	A failing `test_*` cell is a cell in error, so a `write_file` or `edit_file` that breaks a case
    53	reports it in the tool result as a `test_*` cell FAILING, with the assertion's message. A hand-built pass/fail table computes
    54	without error whatever it contains: a failing case is visible only to someone reading the table.
    55	
    56	## Tests over random inputs
    57	
    58	For a claim over many generated inputs ("`unique(xs)` equals `[...new Set(xs)]`",
    59	"`parse(format(x))` equals `x`"). `mulberry32` and `forAll` are copied from `@tomlarkworthy/svg-lens`
    60	(`lopebooks/notebooks/tomlarkworthy_svg-lens.html`), whose `_test_child_laws` makes its rng the same
    61	way. The one change: svg-lens's `forAll(runs, rng, gen, prop, label)` reports the run and the input
    62	but not the seed, so this copy takes a `seed` argument and puts it in the message.
    63	
    64	```js
    65	const _mulberry32 = function _mulberry32(){return(
    66	(seed) => () => {
    67	  seed = (seed + 0x6D2B79F5) | 0;
    68	  let t = seed;
    69	  t = Math.imul(t ^ (t >>> 15), t | 1);
    70	  t ^= t + Math.imul(t ^ (t >>> 7), t | 61);
    71	  return ((t ^ (t >>> 14)) >>> 0) / 4294967296;
    72	}
    73	)};
    74	const _forAll = function _forAll(){return(
    75	(runs, seed, rng, gen, prop, label = "property") => {
    76	  for (let i = 0; i < runs; i++) {
    77	    const args = gen(rng);
    78	    let ok, err;
    79	    try { ok = prop(...args); } catch (e) { ok = false; err = e; }
    80	    if (!ok) throw new Error(label + " counterexample (seed " + seed + ", run " + i + "): " + JSON.stringify(args) + (err ? " — " + err.message : ""));
    81	  }
    82	  return runs + " runs, seed " + seed;
    83	}
    84	)};
    85	const _test_unique_matches_set = function _test_unique_matches_set(forAll, mulberry32, unique){
    86	  const seed = 0x5EED0001;
    87	  const rng = mulberry32(seed);
    88	  const int = (r, min, max) => min + Math.floor(r() * (max - min + 1));
    89	  const gen = (r) => [Array.from({ length: int(r, 0, 12) }, () => int(r, -20, 20))];
    90	  return forAll(200, seed, rng, gen, (xs) =>
    91	    JSON.stringify(unique(xs)) === JSON.stringify([...new Set(xs)]), "unique vs Set");
    92	};
    93	```
    94	
    95	Rules:
    96	
    97	- **Seed the generator; never `Math.random`.** An unseeded test reports a different input on
    98	  every run, and a failure cannot be replayed. Create the rng inside the test cell from a literal
    99	  seed. An rng in a cell of its own is not rerun when the function under test changes, so the
   100	  next run continues its sequence and tests different inputs.
   101	- **The message carries the seed, the run and the input** as JSON, short enough to read, so the
   102	  failing input can be pasted into a one-case test.
   103	- **Check the reference before trusting it.** `Array.prototype.sort()` with no comparator
   104	  compares strings: `[10, 9, -1].sort()` is `[-1, 10, 9]`. Pass `(a, b) => a - b` for numbers.
   105	- **A property must hold for a correct implementation.** Before reporting a failure as a bug in
   106	  the function, run the same property once with the reference in its place (`[...xs].sort(cmp)`
   107	  for a sort, `[...new Set(xs)]` for `unique`). If it fails there too, the test is wrong.
   108	- **Compare the whole result**, element by element (`JSON.stringify` both sides). Equal lengths
   109	  or equal sums pass on most wrong answers.
   110	- **Generate the inputs that break implementations:** empty arrays, duplicates, negative numbers,
   111	  mixed signs, and lengths above 10. For a stability claim, use objects with repeated keys and an
   112	  `id`, since equal numbers cannot show order.

   114	## Testing what a chart or table shows
   115	
   116	Read the element the cell returned, and take the expected value from the data the output is meant
   117	to show, not from the array it was drawn from. Plot gives each mark's `<g>` an `aria-label` naming
   118	the mark (`bar`, `dot`, `line`, `rule`, `frame`), so `g[aria-label='bar'] rect` is one rect per
   119	bar; a bare `rect` also counts a `frame` or a `rect` mark.
   120	
   121	```js
   122	const _test_chart_one_bar_per_month = function _test_chart_one_bar_per_month(chart, sales, d3){
   123	  const months = new Set(sales.map((d) => +d3.utcMonth(d.date))).size;
   124	  const bars = chart.querySelectorAll("g[aria-label='bar'] rect").length;
   125	  if (bars !== months) throw new Error("chart draws " + bars + " bars for " + months + " months in the data");
   126	  return bars + " bars, " + months + " months";
   127	};
   128	```

    10	# Keyboard input, timers and restart in cells
    11	
    12	A game, simulation or animation in a cell has three parts that each go wrong in a Lopecode notebook:
    13	where it listens for keys, how its loop stops, and how it restarts. The notebook page also holds the
    14	chat, the code editor and other modules, and a cell re-runs every time it or an input is edited.
    15	
    16	Observed (robocoop-5, "Make a playable snake game controlled with the arrow keys, with a score and a
    17	restart button", 2026-09-28): the agent put a `keydown` listener on `document` with no
    18	`preventDefault`, started the loop at once, and wired Restart to `location.reload()`. The write
    19	reported "all 10 cells compute with no runtime error". In the page, the arrow keys also scrolled
    20	the page and turned the snake while the user typed in the chat, the snake hit the wall about <T>
    21	after the write, before anyone pressed a key, and Restart reloaded the notebook file. The module had
    22	not been saved, so the reload deleted it.
    23	
    24	## Listen on the element, not the document
    25	
    26	Give the game's root element `tabIndex = 0`, listen for keys on that element, and call
    27	`preventDefault()` only for the keys the game handles. Keys then reach the game only while it has
    28	focus (after a click on it), the arrow keys do not scroll the page, and the chat and editors keep
    29	their keys. `@tomlarkworthy/daw` `keys` (lopebooks/notebooks/tomlarkworthy_daw.html) is a keyboard
    30	widget built this way:
    31	
    32	```js
    33	const el = document.createElement('div');
    34	el.tabIndex = 0;
    35	…
    36	el.addEventListener('keydown', e => {
    37	  if (e.repeat) return;
    38	  const off = keymap[e.code];
    39	  if (off != null) {
    40	    e.preventDefault();
    41	    noteon(base + oct * 12 + off);
    42	    return;
    43	  }
    44	  …
    45	});
    46	el.addEventListener('focus', () => { status.textContent = '⌨ armed (z/x octave)'; });
    47	el.addEventListener('blur', () => { allOff(); status.textContent = 'click to arm ⌨'; });
    48	```
    49	
    50	Show the user that the element must be clicked first ("click to arm"), and do not start a game
    51	until the first key press: a loop that starts on write has usually finished before anyone looks.
    52	
    53	A listener on the element is removed with the element when the cell re-runs. A listener on
    54	`window` or `document` stays on the page after the cell re-runs, so every edit adds another one;
    55	if one is unavoidable, remove it on `invalidation`.
    56	
    57	## Shortcuts with a modifier: match `e.code` or the lower-cased `e.key`
    58	
    59	A page-wide shortcut (Cmd+Shift+L, Cmd+Z) is the exception to listening on an element: it goes on
    60	`document` and is removed on `invalidation`. Holding Shift makes `e.key` the capital letter.
    61	Measured 2026-09-29 in Playwright's Chromium 151 with `page.keyboard.press`:
    62	
    63	```
    64	Meta+Shift+L     key=L code=KeyL
    65	Control+Shift+L  key=L code=KeyL
    66	Shift+KeyL       key=L code=KeyL   (a textarea receives "L")
    67	Meta+KeyL        key=l code=KeyL
    68	```
    69	
    70	A test written as `e.key === 'l' && e.shiftKey` therefore never fires. Compare `e.code` (`'KeyL'`,
    71	the physical key) or `e.key.toLowerCase()`; both hold whatever the case. Not measured: Firefox and
    72	WebKit (not installed for Playwright here), and a physical keypress on macOS, where `key` is set by
    73	the OS rather than by Playwright. `@tomlarkworthy/svg-lens` `toolbar`
    74	(lopebooks/notebooks/tomlarkworthy_svg-lens.html) reads undo and redo from one comparison, with
    75	Shift choosing between them:
    76	
    77	```js
    78	if ((e.metaKey || e.ctrlKey) && e.key.toLowerCase() === 'z' && !typing) {
    79	  e.preventDefault();
    80	  return void (e.shiftKey ? drawing.redo() : drawing.undo());
    81	}
    82	```
    83	
    84	Observed (robocoop-5, "Add a keyboard shortcut, Cmd+Shift+L, that clears this chat and starts a
    85	fresh conversation", 20260929-0620-m56): the agent wrote `ev.key === 'l' && ev.metaKey &&
    86	ev.shiftKey`, reported "The shortcut is live", and the shortcut did nothing when pressed. Until
    87	2026-09-29 `try_control`'s `keys` sent `"Meta+Shift+l"` as key `"l"` and so confirmed that handler;
    88	it now sends the capital letter, as Chromium does.
    89	
    90	A chord with Cmd or Ctrl types no text, so it can also fire while the focus is in a text field. A
    91	shortcut with no modifier, or with Shift alone, must not: a user typing a capital L in a text field
    92	would trigger it. `svg-lens` `toolbar` checks `/^(INPUT|TEXTAREA)$/.test(e.target.tagName) ||
    93	e.target.isContentEditable` for that.
    94	
    95	## Stop the loop on invalidation
    96	
    97	`setInterval`, `setTimeout` chains and `requestAnimationFrame` loops keep running after their cell
    98	re-runs. Each re-run then starts one more loop and the game speeds up. A cell re-runs when any input
    99	changes, so a loop cell that lists a slider value gains a loop on every slider move. Cancel the loop
   100	when the cell is invalidated. `@tomlarkworthy/matrix-background` `_6`
   101	(lopebooks/notebooks/@tomlarkworthy_matrix-background.html) keeps the frame id in a local and ends with:
   102	
   103	```js
   104	invalidation.then(() => {
   105	  if (raf != null) cancelAnimationFrame(raf);
   106	  window.removeEventListener("resize", resize);
   107	});
   108	```
   109	
   110	`@tomlarkworthy/liquid-timer` `mainLoop` does the same with `cancelAnimationFrame(frame)`.
   111	`invalidation` is a built-in: list it as an input of the cell. A generator cell needs no cleanup: the
   112	runtime pulls one value per frame and stops pulling when the cell re-runs (`@tomlarkworthy/lazer-light`
   113	`spring`: `while (true) { …draw…; yield ctx.canvas }`).
   114	
   115	Do not keep the frame id on the cell's function (`<PID>._id`), on `window`, or on another cell's
   116	object, and do not use a "running" flag. Observed (robocoop-5, 20260928-0847-m29, "the animation gets
   117	faster and jerkier every time I move the slider"): the agent stored the id on the cell's compiled
   118	function and cancelled it at the top of the cell. Slider moves then kept one loop, but when the cell was
   119	re-created from its source, as an edit does, the old loop kept running and the new cell produced no
   120	value. A flag on the canvas stopped the extra loops but kept the speed the first loop captured, so the
   121	slider no longer did anything.
   122	
   123	A fix does not stop loops the old code already started: they were never registered on `invalidation`,
   124	so they run until the page is reloaded. Tell the user to save and reopen the notebook to see the fix.
   125	
   126	## Restart by re-running the cell, never by reloading the page
   127	
   128	`location.reload()` reloads the notebook file from disk. Everything not yet saved is lost, including
   129	modules and edits made in this session. To restart, make the cell that holds the game state depend
   130	on a button, so a click re-runs it: the old loop is cancelled on invalidation and the cell builds a
   131	fresh state. `@tomlarkworthy/liquid-timer` does this:
   132	
   133	```js
   134	const _t06 = function _viewof_reset(Inputs){return(
   135	Inputs.button("restart")
   136	)};
   137	const _t07 = (G, _) => G.input(_);
   138	const _t11 = function _liquid(createLiquid,particles,reset)
   139	{
   140	  void reset; // the button rebuilds it
   141	  return createLiquid(particles);
   142	};
   143	// in define():
   144	$def("_t06", "viewof reset", ["Inputs"], _t06);
   145	$def("_t07", "reset", ["Generators","viewof reset"], _t07);
   146	$def("_t11", "liquid", ["createLiquid","particles","reset"], _t11);
   147	```
   148	
   149	`viewof` cells follow `writing-cells-in-module-source.md`.

     8	# Vendoring an npm dependency into a notebook
     9	
    10	Vendoring = the package's bytes live inside the HTML file, so the notebook runs with the network
    11	unplugged. A cell that does `import("https://esm.sh/…")` reads almost identically and is not the same
    12	thing: it works until the reader is offline, or esm.sh is down, or the page is opened from a USB stick.
    13	
    14	## 0. What has to be vendored
    15	
    16	Everything a cell loads from a URL whose content does not change: libraries, and also static data
    17	files published on npm or GitHub (TopoJSON or GeoJSON geometry, a CSV or JSON dataset). Being data
    18	rather than code is not an exemption. In run `20260928-0235-w17-before` (*"Show a world map with the
    19	ten most populous countries highlighted"*) the agent read this page, decided the world-atlas
    20	TopoJSON "is a data file rather than a library", and wrote
    21	
    22	```js
    23	const _world = async function world(d3){return(
    24	  await d3.json("https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/world-atlas@2.0.2/countries-110m.json")
    25	)};
    26	```
    27	
    28	The map was correct online. Reopened with the network blocked, `world` and `topojson` never resolved
    29	and the map was blank. Only a feed whose value changes (weather, prices, a user's own API) stays a
    30	`fetch`.
    31	
    32	A static data file is one `attach_file` and one literal `FileAttachment` call, as in
    33	`@tomlarkworthy/womens-suffrage.<PID>` (`lopebooks/notebooks/@tomlarkworthy_womens-suffrage.html`),
    34	which also carries its world geometry as the attachment `world-110m.v1.json`:
    35	
    36	```
    37	attach_file({ module: "@user/world-map", name: "countries-110m.json",
    38	              url: "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/world-atlas@2.0.2/countries-110m.json" })
    39	```
    40	```js
    41	const <PID> = function _iso3166(FileAttachment){return(
    42	FileAttachment("3166.json").json()
    43	)};
    44	```
    45	
    46	### Builtins that are fetched, not bundled
    47	
    48	Probed 2026-09-28 in the robocoop-5 notebook with every non-`file:` request aborted, one variable per
    49	stdlib builtin. `d3`, `Plot`, `htl`, `Inputs`, `md`, `html`, `svg`, `DOM`, `Generators`, `Mutable`,
    50	`FileAttachment`, `width`, `now` and `_` resolved. These did not:
    51	
    52	```
    53	topojson vl SQLite mermaid L Arrow aq tex dot      → unable to load module   (cdn.jsdelivr.net)
    54	aapl alphabet cars citywages diamonds flare
    55	industries miserables olympians penguins pizza weather → Failed to fetch  (static.observableusercontent.com)
    56	```
    57	
    58	A cell input named `topojson` is therefore a network load, and so is `require("topojson-client@3")`:
    59	the stdlib `require` resolves bare names on cdn.jsdelivr.net. Vendor the library (§ 1, § 2) and
    60	define a cell with the builtin's name in your module, so the cells that use it do not change. A
    61	module's own cell shadows the builtin. topojson-client's `dist/topojson-client.min.js` is UMD; the
    62	CommonJS wrapper of § 2.2 returns its exports:
    63	
    64	```js
    65	const _topojson = async function topojson(FileAttachment){
    66	  const src = await FileAttachment("topojson-client.min.js").text();
    67	  const mod = { exports: {} };
    68	  new Function("module", "exports", "define", src)(mod, mod.exports, undefined);
    69	  return mod.exports;
    70	};
    71	```
    72	
    73	Two separate problems, and they fail differently:
    74	
    75	1. **Storage** — getting the bytes into the one store that both the runtime and the exporter read.
    76	2. **Shape** — most npm packages are not in a form a browser can `import()` at all. This is the part
    77	   that eats the time.
    78	
    79	Everything below with a `→` was measured on 2026-08-30 in
    80	`lopebooks/notebooks/@tomlarkworthy_robocoop-5.html` by `tools/scratch/vendor-pattern-probe.mjs` and
    81	`vendor-pattern-probe2.mjs`, and (the `N` results) by `vendor-fixture-negative-control.mjs`. Error
    82	strings are verbatim.
    83	
    84	## 1. Storage: the runtime FileAttachment map is the only store that counts
    85	
    86	A module's attachments live in a `Map` closed over by its `FileAttachment` builtin.
    87	`@tomlarkworthy/exporter-3` reaches into exactly that map when it serializes:
    88	
    89	```js
    90	const <PID> = function _getFileAttachments(){return(
    91	module => {
    92	  let fileMap;
    93	  const FileAttachment = module._builtins.get('FileAttachment');
    94	  …                                     // monkey-patch Map.prototype.get, call FileAttachment('')
    95	  return fileMap;
    96	}
    97	)};
    98	```
    99	
   100	and `module_specs` emits `<script id="@module/name">` blocks from `getFileAttachments(module)` and
   101	nothing else. So that one `Map` decides **both** whether `FileAttachment("x")` resolves now and
   102	whether the bytes survive an export.
   103	
   104	### The trap: a `<script type="text/plain" id=…>` block is not an attachment
   105	
   106	Bundled libraries *appear* in the file as `<script type="text/plain" id="@user/mod/lib.js.gz">`
   107	blocks, so the obvious move is to write one. Injecting that block genuinely works for
   108	`window.lopecode.contentSync` — `{status: 200, mime: "application/gzip", bytesLen: 322}` — and it is
   109	still wrong twice over: the module's `FileAttachment` map never learns about it, so cells keep
   110	answering
   111	
   112	```
   113	⚠ 2 cells ERRORING at runtime — tinyChunk: File not found: tiny-chunk-3.1.4.js.gz
   114	```
   115	
   116	and exporter-3 never re-emits it, because it reads the map rather than the DOM. Both robocoop-5
   117	baseline runs (2026-08-30) took this route, looped on that error, and scored 0. The block route is a
   118	dead end for vendoring; it is only how *already-exported* attachments happen to be stored.
   119	
   120	### Writing the map at run time
   121	
   122	In a robocoop-5 session, use the `attach_file` tool (added 2026-08-31) — it resolves the owning
   123	module, preserves bytes when given a `url` (so binary/gzip works and the library never passes
   124	through your context), and recomputes erroring cells:
   125	
   126	```
   127	attach_file({ module: "@user/chunker", name: "tiny-chunk.js", url: "https://…/index.js" })
   128	attach_file({ module: "@user/chunker", name: "shim.js", content: "<the transformed source>" })
   129	```
   130	
   131	Everywhere else (pairing `eval_js`, browser console), call `setFileAttachment` directly:
   132	
   133	```js
   134	// eval_js scoped to @tomlarkworthy/fileattachments
   135	const pkgText = await (await fetch(url)).text();
   136	const pkgFile = new File([pkgText], "tiny-chunk.js", { type: "text/javascript" });
   137	await setFileAttachment(pkgFile, window.__ojs_runtime.mains.get("@user/chunker"));
   138	```
   139	
   140	Three things that silently do the wrong thing on the direct route:
   141	
   142	- **`setFileAttachment(file)` attaches to the WRONG module.** Its signature is
   143	  `setFileAttachment(file, module = main)`, and that `main` is `@tomlarkworthy/fileattachments`'s own
   144	  module. Omit the second argument and the write succeeds while `FileAttachment(name)` in your module
   145	  still reports `File not found`. Always pass the owning module.
   146	- **`myModule` from `@tomlarkworthy/runtime-sdk` is not your module** under robocoop-5's apply path —
   147	  probed `{"found":true,"same":false}` against `runtime.mains.get("@user/vendor")`.
   148	  `runtime.mains.get(<module id>)` is the lookup that resolves.
   149	- **`eval_js` binds every cell name your snippet mentions as a parameter**, and `file` IS a cell of
   150	  `@tomlarkworthy/fileattachments` — so a local `const file = …` there dies with
   151	  `syntax error: Identifier 'file' has already been declared`. Name locals `pkgFile`, not `file`.
   152	
   153	Since 2026-08-31, attaching recomputes the module's `FileAttachment`-dependent cells (and
   154	`setFileAttachment` throws if the write cannot be read back). Before that fix the cells stayed in
   155	their `File not found` error until the module file was re-written — see the implicit-variable trap
   156	in `how-file-attachments-work.md`.
   157	
   158	## 2. Shape: what a browser will actually import
   159	
   160	The artifact you attach must be **one file with zero unresolved specifiers**. That is the whole rule,
   161	and it is forced by the blob URL: `import()` of a blob has no hierarchical base, so nothing relative
   162	or bare can resolve from it.
   163	
   164	| you attach | `import(blobUrl)` does | fix |
   165	|---|---|---|
   166	| self-contained ESM | works | none |
   167	| ESM with a bare import | `Failed to resolve module specifier "lodash". Relative references must start with either "/", "./", or "../".` | bundle it |
   168	| ESM with a relative import | `Failed to resolve module specifier "./util.js". Invalid relative url or base scheme isn't hierarchical.` | bundle it, or § 3 |
   169	| UMD, `root` falls back to `this` | `Cannot set properties of undefined (setting 'MyLib')` | § 2.1 |
   170	| UMD, `root` is `typeof self !== "undefined" ? self : this` | **imports clean and exports nothing** — `LOADED []` | § 2.1 |
   171	| CommonJS | `module is not defined` | § 2.2 |
   172	
   173	The second row is why the corpus is full of names like `aws4fetch.esm.js.gz`,
   174	`just-bash.browser.js.gz`, `lezer-lr-bundled.js.gz`, `prosebundle@5.js.gz`,
   175	`isomorphic-git-1@1.30.1.bundle.js.gz` — every one is a pre-bundled single file. Get one from the
   176	package's own `dist/` browser or ESM build, or from a CDN that bundles on demand (jsDelivr `/+esm`,
   177	esm.sh `?bundle`). *(How the existing bundles were produced is recorded only in their file names and
   178	in `@tomlarkworthy/notebook-kit`'s prose — not re-verified here.)*
   179	
   180	`importShim(blobUrl, parentUrl)` does **not** rescue a relative specifier: supplying a parent still
   181	gives `Invalid relative url or base scheme isn't hierarchical`. Do not reach for it.
   182	
   183	### 2.1 UMD
   184	
   185	A UMD bundle never yields exports through `import()` — which of the two failures in the table you get
   186	depends on how its prologue names the global. Evaluate it as a script and read the global instead —
   187	`@tomlarkworthy/p5-sandbox`:
   188	
   189	```js
   190	const text = await (await unzip(FileAttachment("p5.min.js.gz"))).text();
   191	const prevDefine = window.define;
   192	try { window.define = undefined; new Function(text).call(window); }
   193	finally { window.define = prevDefine; }
   194	return window.p5;
   195	```
   196	
   197	That `window.define` dance is load-bearing, and it is a finding rather than superstition: **this page
   198	has an AMD loader**. Probed: `{"define":"function","amd":true}`. A UMD bundle run as-is takes the AMD
   199	branch and the global is never assigned —
   200	
   201	```
   202	UMD with AMD define present     → {"global":null,"defineIsAmd":true}
   203	same UMD inside the wrapper     → {"via":"global"}
   204	```
   205	
   206	The second table row above is the one to watch, and it was found on 2026-08-30 by
   207	`tools/scratch/vendor-fixture-negative-control.mjs` rather than reasoned: the earlier probe used a UMD
   208	whose root fallback is a bare `this`, which is `undefined` in module scope and therefore throws. Most
   209	real bundles instead write `typeof self !== "undefined" ? self : this`, and `self` exists inside a
   210	module — so with an AMD loader on the page the import **succeeds**:
   211	
   212	```
   213	N3 UMD — import paintbox as a module                          LOADED []
   214	N4 UMD — run paintbox as a script WITHOUT shadowing define     {"global":null,"defineIsAmd":true}
   215	```
   216	
   217	`LOADED []` is the dangerous outcome, because nothing throws. A cell that does
   218	`const lib = await import(url)` gets an empty namespace object and fails later, somewhere else, with
   219	`lib.mix is not a function`. If a UMD import returns a namespace with no keys, this is what happened.
   220	
   221	`@tomlarkworthy/claude-code-browser` wraps rather than mutates, which is the safer form because it
   222	never leaves a global clobbered if the bundle throws:
   223	
   224	```js
   225	const wrapped = "(function(define, module, exports){\n" + src + "\n}).call(globalThis, void 0, void 0, void 0);";
   226	```
   227	
   228	`@tomlarkworthy/escodegen` shows a third variant for a bundle whose UMD prologue does not cooperate —
   229	`eval(source.replace(".call(this,this)", ""))`, then `window.escodegen`. Reach for that only when the
   230	wrapper fails; it edits the vendor's bytes and so breaks silently on a version bump.
   231	
   232	### 2.2 CommonJS
   233	
   234	`import()` gives `module is not defined`. Supply the two names it wants:
   235	
   236	```js
   237	const mod = { exports: {} };
   238	new Function("module", "exports", src)(mod, mod.exports);
   239	return mod.exports;
   240	```
   241	
   242	Bundles that are ESM wrappers around a CJS default (`jszip`, `lightning-fs`) import fine but hand you
   243	a namespace object — `@tomlarkworthy/jszip-3-10-1` and `@tomlarkworthy/lightning-fs-4-6-0` both end
   244	`return (await import(objectURL)).default;`. If your cell's value is a namespace with one `default`
   245	key, that is this case.
   246	
   247	## 3. Multi-file packages
   248	
   249	Two routes, and they trade differently.
   250	
   251	**Rewrite the specifier before making the blob.** Attach each file, mint a blob URL for the
   252	dependency, and string-replace the specifier in the entry file:
   253	
   254	```js
   255	const patched = mainSrc.replace('"./util.js"', JSON.stringify(utilUrl));
   256	const m = await import(URL.createObjectURL(new Blob([patched], {type:"text/javascript"})));
   257	→ {"v":"helped"}
   258	```
   259	Works, and it is brittle: it is a textual edit of vendor source, so it must be redone per version and
   260	it does not scale past a handful of files.
   261	
   262	**Or use `<script id>` blocks, where relative specifiers DO resolve.** The notebook's
   263	es-module-shims resolve hook gives block ids a hierarchical namespace, which blob URLs lack:
   264	
   265	```
   266	two blocks @user/plib/index.js + @user/plib/util.js, entry does import {helper} from "./util.js"
   267	  → importShim("@user/plib/index.js")  loaded helped-by-block
   268	bare specifier naming another block (@user/plib2/dep)
   269	  → loaded helped-bare
   270	```
   271	
   272	**Cost, and it is the deciding one:** those blocks are not in any module's `FileAttachment` map, so
   273	by § 1 they do not survive an export. This route is only durable if the same files are ALSO real
   274	attachments of a module — an attachment named `util.js` on `@user/lib` is exported as block id
   275	`@user/lib/util.js`, which is exactly the shape the resolve hook wants. That the two line up is an
   276	inference from the id format, **not tested end-to-end**; the round trip (attach both files → export →
   277	reload → `importShim("@user/lib/index.js")`) is the obvious next experiment and has not been run.
   278	
   279	Recommendation until that is tested: prefer a single bundled file. Reach for multi-file only when
   280	bundling is genuinely impossible, and then use the rewrite route, which is at least known to export.
   281	
   282	### 3.1 A package that runs in a Web Worker (a WASM engine)
   283	
   284	Two limits of the places a notebook runs, each measured in Chromium:
   285	
   286	```
   287	2026-08-09  file:// and GitHub Pages   crossOriginIsolated false, typeof SharedArrayBuffer undefined,
   288	                                       postMessage(shared WebAssembly.Memory) -> DataCloneError
   289	2026-09-26  file://                    new Worker(blobURL, {type: "module"}) fires error at once;
   290	                                       new Worker(blobURL) (classic) and a data: module worker post their message
   291	```
   292	
   293	So a multi-threaded WASM build, which shares memory between its threads, cannot start; take the
   294	package's single-threaded build. The notebook's blob URLs are `blob:null/…`, so a worker built from
   295	an attachment is spawned classic: bundle its entry with esbuild `--format=iife`. A library that
   296	hard-codes `{type: "module"}` needs its worker factory replaced (`tools/monty/monty-module.js` `_pool`
   297	does this for `@pydantic/monty`). A worker that fetches its `.wasm` from a CDN fails offline; hand it
   298	the attachment's bytes or blob URL instead.
   299	
   300	Not tested here: a chess engine specifically. The agent proposed Stockfish 16 in a pairing session
   301	on 2026-09-28 after checking only that the npm package existed; which of its builds are
   302	single-threaded was not checked.
   303	
   304	## 4. Gzip
   305	
   306	Every JS attachment in the corpus is stored gzipped; 49 library attachments across the two content
   307	repos, and the loader is near-identical in all of them:
   308	
   309	```js
   310	const _unzip = function _unzip(Response, DecompressionStream){return(
   311	  async (attachment) =>
   312	    await new Response((await attachment.stream()).pipeThrough(new DecompressionStream("gzip"))).blob()
   313	)};
   314	const _lib = async function lib(unzip, FileAttachment) {
   315	  const blob = await unzip(FileAttachment('mylib.js.gz'));
   316	  const objectURL = URL.createObjectURL(new Blob([blob], { type: 'application/javascript' }));
   317	  try { return await import(objectURL); } finally { URL.revokeObjectURL(objectURL); }
   318	};
   319	```
   320	
   321	Round trip verified in-notebook (`CompressionStream` → `DecompressionStream` → blob → `import`):
   322	`{"gzBytes":45,"v":"gz-ok"}`. Do not use `data-encoding="base64+gzip"` for an attachment — see
   323	`knowledge/how-file-attachments-work.md`.
   324	
   325	`FileAttachment(name)` takes a **literal string only** — Observable static-analyses the call and
   326	rejects `FileAttachment(variable)`. `@tomlarkworthy/assembly-script` works around it with a lookup
   327	table of literal calls:
   328	
   329	```js
   330	const FILES = {
   331	  "binaryen-slim-131.js.gz": FileAttachment("binaryen-slim-131.js.gz"),
   332	  "asc-0.28.20.js.gz":       FileAttachment("asc-0.28.20.js.gz"),
   333	  …
   334	};
   335	```

    13	# Event handlers and buttons in cells: htl.html, not html; a button that acts on another cell's input; a download button; two inputs that update each other; a custom control (pad, canvas); limiting a number box to a range
    14	
    15	A cell that builds a clickable element and passes it a function (`onclick=${() => …}`) must build it
    16	with `htl.html`. The bare `html` built-in in a Lopecode notebook is the legacy stdlib template: it
    17	converts every interpolated value to a string, so the handler never becomes a listener.
    18	
    19	## What `html` does with a function
    20	
    21	Observed (robocoop-5, pomodoro prompt, 2026-09-27): the agent wrote
    22	
    23	```js
    24	const _toggleBtn = function toggleBtn(ru, mru, html){
    25	  return html`<button onclick=${() => { mru.value = !mru.value; }}>${ru ? '⏸ Pause' : '▶ Start'}</button>`;
    26	};
    27	```
    28	
    29	The arrow was stringified into the attribute; the `>` of `=>` ended the tag. The live button had
    30	attributes `onclick="()"` and `==""`, `typeof button.onclick` was `"object"` (null), and its text was
    31	`{ mru.value = !mru.value; }> ▶ Start`. Clicking it did nothing. The write still reported "all 18
    32	cells compute with no runtime error".
    33	
    34	## The form the corpus uses
    35	
    36	`htl.html` binds a function-valued `on…` attribute as an event listener. `@tomlarkworthy/gallery`

    69	## A button that acts on another cell's input
    70	
    71	The action runs once per click and reads the other input's value at click time. The cell holding the
    72	button lists the input's `viewof` and reads `.value` inside the click function.
    73	`@tomlarkworthy/editor-5` `up` (in 224 notebook files, e.g. lopebooks/notebooks/@tomlarkworthy_robocoop-5.html)
    74	reads `viewof editedCell` this way:
    75	
    76	```js

    78	Inputs.button("⬆", {
    79	  reduce: () => moveCell($0.value, -1)

    81	)};

    86	The same `$0.value` read works inside an `htl.html` `onclick=${…}` function. When other cells show the
    87	result, `reduce` can return it (or a promise of it): the button's value cell then changes once per
    88	click, and cells that list it recompute once per click.

    93	- **The action cell lists the text's value cell** (`"inputText"`). It re-runs on every keystroke, so
    94	  the request is sent while the user types, and the button does nothing the text had not already done.

   140	## Listening on an Inputs view; two inputs that update each other
   141	
   142	An `Inputs.*` view (`Inputs.number`, `Inputs.text`, `Inputs.range`, …) is a `<form>` that wraps a
   143	label and the control. It is not the `<input>`. The view has `value` (read and write), and `input`
   144	events from the control bubble up to it. `document.activeElement` is never the view, because focus is
   145	on the `<input>` inside it, and the view has no `valueAsNumber`. The inner element is
   146	`view.querySelector("input")`.
   147	
   148	Observed (robocoop-5, temperature converter, 20260928-0510-w25): the agent guarded each listener with
   149	`document.activeElement === viewof_celsius` and read `viewof_celsius.valueAsNumber`. The guard was
   150	always false, so typing in either box changed nothing. The write reported "all 10 cells compute with
   151	no runtime error", and the agent told the user the converter worked. With the guard changed to
   152	`viewof_celsius.contains(document.activeElement)` and `.valueAsNumber` changed to `.value`, the same
   153	module passed.
   154	
   155	Two controls that show one quantity: keep the quantity in one hidden state cell,
   156	`viewof celsius = Inputs.input(20)`, and bind each control to it. `Inputs.bind(target, source)` copies
   157	`source.value` into the control, and on the control's `input` event writes the value back to the state
   158	and dispatches `input` on it, so the `celsius` value cell and every other bound control update. The
   159	corpus binds a second control to an existing view this way: `@tomlarkworthy/dataflow-templating` `_dtv2j`
   160	(lopecode/notebooks/@tomlarkworthy_atlas.html) is `Inputs.bind(Inputs.range([1, 4], { label: "widgets",
   161	step: 1 }), $0)` on `viewof widgetCount`. `Inputs.bind` copies values unchanged, so a control that
   162	shows a converted value needs a bind with a function each way:
   163	
   164	```js
   165	const _celsius = function celsius(Inputs){return( Inputs.input(20) )};
   166	const _bindVia = function bindVia(){return(
   167	(target, source, to, from, invalidation) => {
   168	  let fromTarget = false;
   169	  const onSource = () => { if (!fromTarget) target.value = to(source.value); };
   170	  const onTarget = () => {
   171	    if (!Number.isFinite(target.value)) return;
   172	    fromTarget = true;
   173	    source.value = from(target.value);
   174	    source.dispatchEvent(new Event("input", {bubbles: true}));
   175	    fromTarget = false;
   176	  };
   177	  onSource();
   178	  target.addEventListener("input", onTarget);
   179	  source.addEventListener("input", onSource);
   180	  invalidation?.then(() => source.removeEventListener("input", onSource));
   181	  return target;
   182	}
   183	)};
   184	const _cBox = function cBox(Inputs, $celsius, invalidation){return(
   185	  Inputs.bind(Inputs.number({label: "Celsius (°C)"}), $celsius, invalidation)
   186	)};
   187	const _fBox = function fBox(Inputs, bindVia, $celsius, invalidation){return(
   188	  bindVia(Inputs.number({label: "Fahrenheit (°F)"}), $celsius,
   189	    c => Math.round((c * 9 / 5 + 32) * 100) / 100, f => (f - 32) * 5 / 9, invalidation)
   190	)};
   191	// in define():
   192	$def("_celsius", "viewof celsius", ["Inputs"], _celsius);
   193	main.variable(observer("celsius")).define("celsius", ["Generators", "viewof celsius"], (G, _) => G.input(_));
   194	$def("_bindVia", "bindVia", [], _bindVia);
   195	$def("_cBox", "cBox", ["Inputs", "viewof celsius", "invalidation"], _cBox);
   196	$def("_fBox", "fBox", ["Inputs", "bindVia", "viewof celsius", "invalidation"], _fBox);
   197	```
   198	
   199	The control cells list `viewof celsius`, not `celsius`, so they are not rebuilt on each keystroke.
   200	Setting `.value` dispatches no event, so writes do not echo. `fromTarget` stops the state's `input`
   201	event from rewriting the box being typed in: without it, typing `98.60` in °F was reformatted to `98.6`
   202	under the cursor (probe `tools/scratch/rc5-sessions/s37-shared-state-bind.mjs`, 2026-09-28). With it,
   203	typing °F=212, °C=-40, °F=98.6 gave `celsius` 100, -40, 37, the other box 100, -40, 37, and the typed
   204	text kept each time.
   205	
   206	A listener cell that writes each box's converted value into the other box's `.value` also passes the
   207	converter eval, and this page recommended it until 2026-09-28. It leaves no single value to depend
   208	on: the `fahrenheit` value cell does not update when °C is typed, because setting `.value` dispatches
   209	nothing (follows from the no-echo behaviour above; not measured separately).
   210	
   211	## A custom control: set `.value`, then dispatch `input`
   212	
   213	A `viewof` cell can return any element: a pad, a canvas, an svg. The runtime reads the element's
   214	`.value` when the element dispatches `input`, so the value has to be set before the event:
   215	
   216	```js
   217	el.addEventListener("pointerdown", () => {
   218	  el.value = el.value + 1;                              // first
   219	  el.dispatchEvent(new Event("input", {bubbles: true})); // then
   220	});
   221	```
   222	
   223	Observed (robocoop-5 pairing, drum pad, 2026-09-28): the agent's pad dispatched `input` and then set
   224	`.value`, so each hit showed the previous hit's value. Every cell computed and the write reported no
   225	error. The user found it by playing the pad. `try_control` now presses a custom control with the
   226	pointer (down, up, click at its centre) when no `value` is given, and names this cause when the
   227	element's `.value` moved but the value cell did not. Probe `tools/scratch/rc5-sessions/s69-try-control-presses-custom-view.mjs`
   228	builds both orders: the lagging pad is flagged, the other reports `hits 0 → 1`.
   229	
   230	`setPointerCapture` inside a synthetic or already-released pointer event throws `NotFoundError`
   231	(seen in the same session, uncaught). Wrap it in `try`, or leave it out for a press that does not drag.
   232	
   233	## Limiting a number box: the range is the first argument
   234	
   235	`Inputs.number([min, max], options)` and `Inputs.range([min, max], options)` take the limits as the
   236	first argument. There is no `min` or `max` option: `Inputs.number({min: 0, max: 500})` ignores both
   237	without an error (`createRange` in `vendor/observable-inputs/src/range.js` destructures `extent:
   238	[min, max]` from the first argument and never reads `options.min`). `Inputs.range({min, max})`
   239	throws `object is not iterable`.
   240	
   241	Typed into the box the way a user does (probe `tools/scratch/rc5-train/20260928-0847/m31/inputs-behaviour.mjs`,
   242	2026-09-28, the Inputs shipped in robocoop-5):
   243	
   244	```
   245	typed   Inputs.number({min: 0, max: 500, value: 100})   Inputs.number([0, 500], {value: 100})
   246	-5      value -5, box valid                             value stays 100, box :invalid
   247	600     value 600, box valid                            value stays 100, box :invalid
   248	""      value unchanged, box :invalid                   value stays 100, box :invalid
   249	250     value 250                                       value 250
   250	```
   251	
   252	With the extent, an out-of-range, empty or non-numeric entry keeps the last good value and
   253	dispatches nothing, so dependent cells do not recompute; the box shows the entry the value does not
   254	have. A cell that should say what is wrong has to read the box itself
   255	(`viewof x.querySelector("input")`) or take `Inputs.text` and parse it.
   256	
   257	Observed (rc5-train m26, 2026-09-28, "make the AQI converter handle bad input"): in 3 of 3 runs the
   258	agent wrote `Inputs.number({ label: "AQI", value: 100, step: 1, min: 0, max: 500 })` and told the
   259	user the box now refuses values outside 0–500. It accepted -5 and 600.
   260	
   261	The corpus form, `@tomlarkworthy/inputs-reference._number_example`
   262	(lopebooks/notebooks/@tomlarkworthy_inputs-reference.html):
   263	
   264	```js
   265	Inputs.number([0, 10000], { label: 'price', value: 99, step: 0.01 })
   266	```
   267	
   268	A one-sided limit is `Inputs.number([0, Infinity], …)`: a non-finite or `null` end is no limit
   269	(`range.js`, `if (max == null || isNaN(max = +max)) max = Infinity`).

     7	# Keeping user state in the saved notebook file (localStorage does not travel)
     8	
     9	A Lopecode notebook is one HTML file. "It should still be there next time I open the notebook" means
    10	the state is written into that file when the notebook is saved (Save in place, or export), so it
    11	reopens with the file: in another browser, on another machine, or after the file is emailed.
    12	
    13	`localStorage`, `sessionStorage` and IndexedDB are none of these. They belong to one browser profile
    14	and one origin, are not part of the file, and throw on an opaque origin (a `blob:` fork). Use them
    15	only for per-browser settings that must *not* travel with the file: API keys, a model choice, a
    16	panel toggle. The corpus uses them for exactly that (`@tomlarkworthy/local-storage-view`, the
    17	robocoop-5 model picker and key field).
    18	
    19	Observed (run 20260927-2352-w6, todo-list prompt): the agent kept the list in
    20	`localStorage.getItem("todo-list")` and reported that items "persist across page reloads and
    21	notebook reopenings". After an export and a reopen in a fresh browser context, the list was empty.

    23	## JSON state: `sticky` rewrites the cell's own source
    24	
    25	`@tomlarkworthy/sticky` wraps any view. The second argument is a literal slot; on every `input`
    26	event from the view, sticky writes `JSON.stringify(view.value)` into that slot in the cell's
    27	definition. Saving the notebook saves the source, so the value comes back on reopen.
    28	
    29	From `@tomlarkworthy/codestrates.doc` (lopebooks `tomlarkworthy_codestrates.html`), a whole HTML
    30	document kept this way:
    31	
    32	```js
    33	const <PID> = function _doc(sticky,codestrate,defaultCodestrate) {return (sticky(codestrate({ value: defaultCodestrate }), "<!doctype html>…"))};
    34	```
    35	
    36	Module source for a list, with the import (sticky is fetched from observablehq.com on first write
    37	and embedded in the file from then on):
    38	
    39	```js
    40	const _viewof_todos = function viewof_todos(sticky, todoList){return( sticky(todoList(), []) )};
    41	…
    42	  $def("_viewof_todos", "viewof todos", ["sticky", "todoList"], _viewof_todos);
    43	  $def("_todos", "todos", ["Generators", "viewof todos"], (G, v) => G.input(v));
    44	  main.define("module @tomlarkworthy/sticky", async () => runtime.module((await import("/@tomlarkworthy/sticky.js?v=4")).default));
    45	  main.define("sticky", ["module @tomlarkworthy/sticky", "@variable"], (_, v) => v.import("sticky", _));
    46	```
    47	
    48	The view must follow the Observable view contract, because sticky only talks to it through that.
    49	Sticky restores a saved value by **assigning `el.value` when the cell runs**, so the setter must
    50	re-render. A setter that only stores the value leaves the reopened list blank while the data is in
    51	the source. From `@tomlarkworthy/codestrates.codestratePlace` (lopebooks
    52	`tomlarkworthy_codestrates.html`, used as `sticky(codestratePlace($0))`):
    53	
    54	```js
    55	  Object.defineProperty(root, "value", {
    56	    get: () => state,
    57	    set: (v) => {
    58	      state = { where: v?.where === "webstrate" && v?.url ? "webstrate" : "notebook", url: v?.url || "" };
    59	      render();
    60	    }
    61	  });
    62	  render();
    63	  return root;
    64	```

    66	- `get` returns the state, JSON-serializable (arrays, objects, strings, numbers).
    67	- `set` replaces the state **and calls `render()`**.
    68	- after each user edit, `el.dispatchEvent(new Event("input", {bubbles: true}))`; sticky writes the
    69	  slot on that event.

    71	`Inputs.*` widgets already satisfy this: `sticky(Inputs.range([0, 100], {value: 50}), 50)`.

    74	attachment instead (`how-file-attachments-work.md`).

    13	# Event handlers and buttons in cells: htl.html, not html; a button that acts on another cell's input; a download button; two inputs that update each other; a custom control (pad, canvas); limiting a number box to a range
    14	
    15	A cell that builds a clickable element and passes it a function (`onclick=${() => …}`) must build it
    16	with `htl.html`. The bare `html` built-in in a Lopecode notebook is the legacy stdlib template: it
    17	converts every interpolated value to a string, so the handler never becomes a listener.
    18	
    19	## What `html` does with a function
    20	
    21	Observed (robocoop-5, pomodoro prompt, 2026-09-27): the agent wrote
    22	
    23	```js
    24	const _toggleBtn = function toggleBtn(ru, mru, html){
    25	  return html`<button onclick=${() => { mru.value = !mru.value; }}>${ru ? '⏸ Pause' : '▶ Start'}</button>`;
    26	};
    27	```
    28	
    29	The arrow was stringified into the attribute; the `>` of `=>` ended the tag. The live button had
    30	attributes `onclick="()"` and `==""`, `typeof button.onclick` was `"object"` (null), and its text was
    31	`{ mru.value = !mru.value; }> ▶ Start`. Clicking it did nothing. The write still reported "all 18
    32	cells compute with no runtime error".

    34	## The form the corpus uses
    35	
    36	`htl.html` binds a function-valued `on…` attribute as an event listener. `@tomlarkworthy/gallery`
    37	`card` (lopebooks/notebooks/@tomlarkworthy_gallery.html) writes a mutable from a button this way:
    38	
    39	```js
    40	htl.html`<button class="card-star" onclick=${(e) => {
    41	  e.stopPropagation();
    42	  const current = new Map($edits.value);
    43	  …
    44	  $edits.value = current;
    45	}}>${featured ? "★" : "☆"}</button>`

    47	
    48	`$edits` is that cell's name for its `"mutable edits"` input. The same shape in a module file, for a
    49	start/pause toggle:
    50	
    51	```js
    52	const _toggle = function toggle(htl, running, $running){return(
    53	  htl.html`<button onclick=${() => { $running.value = !running; }}>${running ? "Pause" : "Start"}</button>`
    54	)};
    55	// in define():
    56	$def("_toggle", "toggle", ["htl", "running", "mutable running"], _toggle);
    57	```

    59	`htl` is a built-in: list it as an input, as with `md` or `Inputs`. `@tomlarkworthy/lopecode-tour`
    60	`ui_prose` (lopecode/notebooks/@tomlarkworthy_lopecode-tour.html) has a smaller example:
    61	`htl.html\`<button onclick=${(e) => {e.target.innerHTML = "thanks"; e.stopPropagation()}}>click me!</button>\``.

    69	## A button that acts on another cell's input
    70	
    71	The action runs once per click and reads the other input's value at click time. The cell holding the
    72	button lists the input's `viewof` and reads `.value` inside the click function.
    73	`@tomlarkworthy/editor-5` `up` (in 224 notebook files, e.g. lopebooks/notebooks/@tomlarkworthy_robocoop-5.html)
    74	reads `viewof editedCell` this way:
    75	
    76	```js
    77	const <PID> = function _up(Inputs,moveCell,$0){return(
    78	Inputs.button("⬆", {
    79	  reduce: () => moveCell($0.value, -1)
    80	})
    81	)};
    82	// in define():
    83	$def("<PID>", "viewof up", ["Inputs","moveCell","viewof editedCell"], <PID>);
    84	```
    85	
    86	The same `$0.value` read works inside an `htl.html` `onclick=${…}` function. When other cells show the
    87	result, `reduce` can return it (or a promise of it): the button's value cell then changes once per
    88	click, and cells that list it recompute once per click.
