   114	## A button that downloads a file
   115	
   116	The cell's value is the button. The file is built and saved inside its click handler, so nothing is
   117	saved until it is clicked. The cell may list the values the file is made from; when they change the
   118	cell returns a new button and saves nothing. `@tomlarkworthy/suminagashi` `_download`
   119	(lopebooks/notebooks/@tomlarkworthy_suminagashi.html) saves a PNG this way. The same shape for a CSV:
   120	
   121	```js
   122	const _saveCsv = function saveCsv(htl, d3, rows){return(
   123	  htl.html`<button onclick=${() => {
   124	    const blob = new Blob([d3.csvFormat(rows)], {type: "text/csv"});
   125	    const link = htl.html`<a download="rows.csv" href=${URL.createObjectURL(blob)}>`;
   126	    link.click();
   127	    setTimeout(() => URL.revokeObjectURL(link.href), 1000);
   128	  }}>Download CSV</button>`
   129	)};

   131	$def("_saveCsv", "saveCsv", ["htl", "d3", "rows"], _saveCsv);
   132	```
   133	
   134	An async builder (a zip, a PDF) goes inside the handler: `onclick=${async () => { const blob = await build(rows); … }}`.
   135	The stdlib `DOM.download(blob, name, label)` returns a ready control too
   136	(`@tomlarkworthy/fileattachments` `_download_selected`, lopecode/notebooks/@tomlarkworthy_atlas.html);
   137	its first click builds the file and relabels the button "Download"; a second click saves it
   138	(`download.js` in the stdlib awaits the value before it sets `href`).
   139	
   140	## Listening on an Inputs view; two inputs that update each other
   141	
   142	An `Inputs.*` view (`Inputs.number`, `Inputs.text`, `Inputs.range`, …) is a `<form>` that wraps a
   143	label and the control. It is not the `<input>`. The view has `value` (read and write), and `input`
   144	events from the control bubble up to it. `document.activeElement` is never the view, because focus is
   145	on the `<input>` inside it, and the view has no `valueAsNumber`. The inner element is
   146	`view.querySelector("input")`.
   147	
   148	Observed (robocoop-5, temperature converter, 20260928-0510-w25): the agent guarded each listener with
   149	`document.activeElement === viewof_celsius` and read `viewof_celsius.valueAsNumber`. The guard was
   150	always false, so typing in either box changed nothing. The write reported "all 10 cells compute with
   151	no runtime error", and the agent told the user the converter worked. With the guard changed to
   152	`viewof_celsius.contains(document.activeElement)` and `.valueAsNumber` changed to `.value`, the same
   153	module passed.
   154	
   155	Two controls that show one quantity: keep the quantity in one hidden state cell,
   156	`viewof celsius = Inputs.input(20)`, and bind each control to it. `Inputs.bind(target, source)` copies
   157	`source.value` into the control, and on the control's `input` event writes the value back to the state
   158	and dispatches `input` on it, so the `celsius` value cell and every other bound control update. The
   159	corpus binds a second control to an existing view this way: `@tomlarkworthy/dataflow-templating` `_dtv2j`
   160	(lopecode/notebooks/@tomlarkworthy_atlas.html) is `Inputs.bind(Inputs.range([1, 4], { label: "widgets",
   161	step: 1 }), $0)` on `viewof widgetCount`. `Inputs.bind` copies values unchanged, so a control that
   162	shows a converted value needs a bind with a function each way:
   163	
   164	```js
   165	const _celsius = function celsius(Inputs){return( Inputs.input(20) )};
   166	const _bindVia = function bindVia(){return(
   167	(target, source, to, from, invalidation) => {
   168	  let fromTarget = false;
   169	  const onSource = () => { if (!fromTarget) target.value = to(source.value); };
   170	  const onTarget = () => {
   171	    if (!Number.isFinite(target.value)) return;
   172	    fromTarget = true;
   173	    source.value = from(target.value);
   174	    source.dispatchEvent(new Event("input", {bubbles: true}));
   175	    fromTarget = false;
   176	  };
   177	  onSource();
   178	  target.addEventListener("input", onTarget);
   179	  source.addEventListener("input", onSource);
   180	  invalidation?.then(() => source.removeEventListener("input", onSource));
   181	  return target;
   182	}
   183	)};
   184	const _cBox = function cBox(Inputs, $celsius, invalidation){return(
   185	  Inputs.bind(Inputs.number({label: "Celsius (°C)"}), $celsius, invalidation)
   186	)};
   187	const _fBox = function fBox(Inputs, bindVia, $celsius, invalidation){return(
   188	  bindVia(Inputs.number({label: "Fahrenheit (°F)"}), $celsius,
   189	    c => Math.round((c * 9 / 5 + 32) * 100) / 100, f => (f - 32) * 5 / 9, invalidation)
   190	)};
   191	// in define():
   192	$def("_celsius", "viewof celsius", ["Inputs"], _celsius);
   193	main.variable(observer("celsius")).define("celsius", ["Generators", "viewof celsius"], (G, _) => G.input(_));
   194	$def("_bindVia", "bindVia", [], _bindVia);
   195	$def("_cBox", "cBox", ["Inputs", "viewof celsius", "invalidation"], _cBox);
   196	$def("_fBox", "fBox", ["Inputs", "bindVia", "viewof celsius", "invalidation"], _fBox);
   197	```
   198	
   199	The control cells list `viewof celsius`, not `celsius`, so they are not rebuilt on each keystroke.
   200	Setting `.value` dispatches no event, so writes do not echo. `fromTarget` stops the state's `input`
   201	event from rewriting the box being typed in: without it, typing `98.60` in °F was reformatted to `98.6`
   202	under the cursor (probe `tools/scratch/rc5-sessions/s37-shared-state-bind.mjs`, 2026-09-28). With it,
   203	typing °F=212, °C=-40, °F=98.6 gave `celsius` 100, -40, 37, the other box 100, -40, 37, and the typed
   204	text kept each time.
   205	
   206	A listener cell that writes each box's converted value into the other box's `.value` also passes the
   207	converter eval, and this page recommended it until 2026-09-28. It leaves no single value to depend
   208	on: the `fahrenheit` value cell does not update when °C is typed, because setting `.value` dispatches
   209	nothing (follows from the no-echo behaviour above; not measured separately).

   211	## A custom control: set `.value`, then dispatch `input`
   212	
   213	A `viewof` cell can return any element: a pad, a canvas, an svg. The runtime reads the element's
   214	`.value` when the element dispatches `input`, so the value has to be set before the event:
   215	
   216	```js
   217	el.addEventListener("pointerdown", () => {
   218	  el.value = el.value + 1;                              // first
   219	  el.dispatchEvent(new Event("input", {bubbles: true})); // then
   220	});
   221	```
   222	
   223	Observed (robocoop-5 pairing, drum pad, 2026-09-28): the agent's pad dispatched `input` and then set
   224	`.value`, so each hit showed the previous hit's value. Every cell computed and the write reported no
   225	error. The user found it by playing the pad. `try_control` now presses a custom control with the
   226	pointer (down, up, click at its centre) when no `value` is given, and names this cause when the
   227	element's `.value` moved but the value cell did not. Probe `tools/scratch/rc5-sessions/s69-try-control-presses-custom-view.mjs`
   228	builds both orders: the lagging pad is flagged, the other reports `hits 0 → 1`.
   229	
   230	`setPointerCapture` inside a synthetic or already-released pointer event throws `NotFoundError`
   231	(seen in the same session, uncaught). Wrap it in `try`, or leave it out for a press that does not drag.
   232	
   233	## Limiting a number box: the range is the first argument
   234	
   235	`Inputs.number([min, max], options)` and `Inputs.range([min, max], options)` take the limits as the
   236	first argument. There is no `min` or `max` option: `Inputs.number({min: 0, max: 500})` ignores both
   237	without an error (`createRange` in `vendor/observable-inputs/src/range.js` destructures `extent:
   238	[min, max]` from the first argument and never reads `options.min`). `Inputs.range({min, max})`
   239	throws `object is not iterable`.
   240	
   241	Typed into the box the way a user does (probe `tools/scratch/rc5-train/20260928-0847/m31/inputs-behaviour.mjs`,
   242	2026-09-28, the Inputs shipped in robocoop-5):
   243	
   244	```
   245	typed   Inputs.number({min: 0, max: 500, value: 100})   Inputs.number([0, 500], {value: 100})
   246	-5      value -5, box valid                             value stays 100, box :invalid
   247	600     value 600, box valid                            value stays 100, box :invalid
   248	""      value unchanged, box :invalid                   value stays 100, box :invalid
   249	250     value 250                                       value 250
   250	```
   251	
   252	With the extent, an out-of-range, empty or non-numeric entry keeps the last good value and
   253	dispatches nothing, so dependent cells do not recompute; the box shows the entry the value does not
   254	have. A cell that should say what is wrong has to read the box itself
   255	(`viewof x.querySelector("input")`) or take `Inputs.text` and parse it.
   256	
   257	Observed (rc5-train m26, 2026-09-28, "make the AQI converter handle bad input"): in 3 of 3 runs the
   258	agent wrote `Inputs.number({ label: "AQI", value: 100, step: 1, min: 0, max: 500 })` and told the
   259	user the box now refuses values outside 0–500. It accepted -5 and 600.
   260	
   261	The corpus form, `@tomlarkworthy/inputs-reference._number_example`
   262	(lopebooks/notebooks/@tomlarkworthy_inputs-reference.html):
   263	
   264	```js
   265	Inputs.number([0, 10000], { label: 'price', value: 99, step: 0.01 })
   266	```
   267	
   268	A one-sided limit is `Inputs.number([0, Infinity], …)`: a non-finite or `null` end is no limit
   269	(`range.js`, `if (max == null || isNaN(max = +max)) max = Infinity`).

     7	
     8	# Reading a whole list from a paged web API
     9	
    10	A list endpoint (a user's repos, issues, records, search results) returns one page. Anything
    11	computed over "all of them" (a total, a top 10, a breakdown) is wrong when only the first page was
    12	read, and nothing errors: the cells compute and the numbers look plausible.
    13	
    14	## One request is one page
    15	
    16	Measured on api.github.com, unauthenticated, 2026-09-28:
    17	
    18	```
    19	/users/sindresorhus                                      public_repos 1141
    20	/users/sindresorhus/repos?per_page=100&sort=stars&direction=desc
    21	   100 repos, 22,384 stars, top repo awesome-chatgpt 6,421
    22	   link: <.../user/170270/repos?per_page=100&sort=stars&direction=desc&page=2>; rel="next", <...&page=12>; rel="last"
    23	/search/repositories?q=user:sindresorhus&sort=stars&order=desc&per_page=10
    24	   top repo awesome 511,507
    25	```
    26	
    27	- `per_page` defaults to 30 and stops at 100 (GitHub's docs; the 100 page above is consistent).
    28	- `sort=stars` is not a sort `/users/{u}/repos` accepts (it takes `created`, `updated`, `pushed`,
    29	  `full_name`). It is ignored without an error, so the 100 repos above are not the 100 most starred
    30	  and the real top repo, `awesome`, is not among them.
    31	- An account under 100 repos (`mbostock`, 88) fits in one page, so testing with a small account
    32	  hides the defect.
    33	
    34	In run 20260928-0600-w30-before (robocoop-5, mimo-v2.5-pro) the agent built a GitHub dashboard with
    35	one `per_page=100` request, tested it on `torvalds`, and reported it "fully working". For a
    36	130-repo user it printed "has 100 public repos with a total of 297 stars" and charted ten
    37	low-star repos (the 130-repo user is the eval's emulated GitHub, `rc5t-github-dashboard`).
    38	
    39	## Follow the pages
    40	
    41	Loop until the API says there are no more, with a bound on the number of pages. The corpus form is
    42	`@tomlarkworthy/at-write._knownCidsFromPds` (lopebooks/notebooks/Feeling_of_Computing.html), which
    43	follows a `cursor` with `maxPages`:
    44	
    45	```js
    46	let cursor = null;
    47	for (let page = 0; page < maxPages; page++) {
    48	  const q = new URLSearchParams({ did, limit: '1000', ...cursor ? { cursor } : {} });
    49	  const r = await fetch(`${ pds }/xrpc/com.atproto.sync.listBlobs?${ q }`);
    50	  if (!r.ok) break;
    51	  const data = await r.json();
    52	  for (const c of data.cids || []) known.add(String(c));
    53	  cursor = data.cursor;
    54	  if (!cursor || !(data.cids || []).length) break;
    55	}
    56	```
    57	
    58	GitHub signals the next page in the `Link` response header rather than the body:
    59	
    60	```js
    61	let url = `https://api.github.com/users/${encodeURIComponent(login)}/repos?per_page=100`;
    62	for (let page = 0; url && page < 30; page++) {
    63	  const r = await fetch(url);
    64	  if (!r.ok) { /* return a message value, see below */ }
    65	  repos.push(...await r.json());
    66	  url = (/<([^>]+)>;\s*rel="next"/.exec(r.headers.get("link") || "") || [])[1];
    67	}
    68	```
    69	
    70	Check the count you got against one the API states when there is one (`public_repos` on
    71	`/users/{u}`); say "first N of M" in the output if the bound was hit.
    72	
    73	For "top N by X" only, a search endpoint that sorts server-side can answer in one request
    74	(`/search/repositories?q=user:{u}&sort=stars&per_page=10` above). It does not give a total over
    75	every item, and GitHub's search has its own budget (10 requests a minute unauthenticated, per
    76	GitHub's docs; not measured here).
    77	
    78	## Every page is a request against the rate limit
    79	
    80	Unauthenticated GitHub allows 60 requests an hour per IP (`x-ratelimit-limit: 60` on every
    81	response). A 1141-repo user costs 12 of them. An `Inputs.text` without `submit` changes its value
    82	on every keystroke, so typing `torvalds` looks up `t`, `to`, … `torvald` first: in the w30 replay
    83	that was 7 wasted lookups per name. Use `submit: true` so the value changes on Enter or the
    84	button, as `@tomlarkworthy/viewroutine.newName` does (lopebooks/notebooks/@tomlarkworthy_rss-feed.html):
    85	
    86	```js
    87	Inputs.text({
    88	  label: "please enter the name of the thing to create",
    89	  submit: true,
    90	  minlength: 1
    91	})
    92	```
    93	
    94	When the budget is spent GitHub answers 403 (or 429, per its docs) with `x-ratelimit-remaining: 0`
    95	and `x-ratelimit-reset` in epoch seconds. Return that as a value the page shows ("rate limit
    96	reached, try again after 16:05"), not a thrown error; `@tomlarkworthy/foc-wiki._wikiPulls`
    97	(Feeling_of_Computing.html) returns `{ ok: false, error: msg, remaining: r.headers.get("x-ratelimit-remaining") }`.
    98	The 403 body and headers here are from GitHub's documentation, not from a captured response.

     9	# Writing viewof, mutable and import cells in module source
    10	
    11	A module file under `/src` is the compiled `define()` form, not Observable source. Three Observable
    12	constructs expand into more than one variable there, and each must be written out in full. The
    13	robocoop-5 agent got every one of these wrong at least once on 2026-09-27; the failures are quoted
    14	under each.
    15	
    16	## viewof — two variables
    17	
    18	```js
    19	$def("_k1", "viewof knob", ["Inputs"], (Inputs) => Inputs.range([0, 100], {value: 10}));
    20	$def("_k2", "knob", ["Generators", "viewof knob"], (G, v) => G.input(v));
    21	```
    22	
    23	`knob` is the value; other cells list `"knob"` as an input and recompute when the slider moves.
    24	`Generators.input` is what connects the two: it yields the element's `value` on every `input`
    25	event.
    26	
    27	Observed (e6, game-theory prompt): the value cell was written as `(viewof_marketSize) =>
    28	viewof_marketSize`, so `marketSize` was the element, and every payoff came out `NaN`. The fix the
    29	agent chose, `+viewof_marketSize.value`, reads the slider once when the cell first runs and never
    30	again: the model stopped responding to its own inputs. Both compile and both report "computes
    31	with no runtime error", so the apply result does not catch either.
    32	
    33	## mutable — three variables
    34	
    35	```js
    36	$def("_m1", "initial count", [], () => 0);
    37	$def("_m2", "mutable count", ["Mutable", "initial count"], (M, _) => new M(_));
    38	$def("_m3", "count", ["mutable count"], _ => _.generator);
    39	```
    40	
    41	Read `count` to react to it. Assign through `"mutable count"` (`m.value = 5`). Copied from the
    42	`item` cell of `@spond/revised-sars-cov-2-analytics-page` in lopebooks.
    43	
    44	## import — a loader and a binding per name
    45	
    46	```js
    47	main.define("module @user/other", async () => runtime.module((await import("/@user/other.js?v=4")).default));
    48	main.define("x", ["module @user/other", "@variable"], (_, v) => v.import("x", _));
    49	```
    50	
    51	Both lines go inside `define()`, after the `$def` lines. The same two lines load a notebook
    52	published on observablehq.com that this page does not embed; after the write applies, its source
    53	is readable at `/src/@user/other.js`. To read a published notebook's API before importing it, fetch
    54	`https://api.observablehq.com/@user/other.js?v=4`. `?v=3`, `/d/…` and the observablehq.com page URL
    55	were all tried in runs on 2026-09-27 and none returned the module.

    57	Observed: before lopebooks `dd9a6f7f` the apply bound an import of a notebook not in the page to an
    58	empty module of the same name, so every imported name was "not defined" although the file was
    59	correct. If an import still reports a name as not defined, check the loader line's path before
    60	rewriting the binding.

     5	---
     6	
     7	# Keeping user state in the saved notebook file (localStorage does not travel)
     8	
     9	A Lopecode notebook is one HTML file. "It should still be there next time I open the notebook" means
    10	the state is written into that file when the notebook is saved (Save in place, or export), so it
    11	reopens with the file: in another browser, on another machine, or after the file is emailed.
    12	
    13	`localStorage`, `sessionStorage` and IndexedDB are none of these. They belong to one browser profile
    14	and one origin, are not part of the file, and throw on an opaque origin (a `blob:` fork). Use them
    15	only for per-browser settings that must *not* travel with the file: API keys, a model choice, a
    16	panel toggle. The corpus uses them for exactly that (`@tomlarkworthy/local-storage-view`, the
    17	robocoop-5 model picker and key field).
    18	
    19	Observed (run 20260927-2352-w6, todo-list prompt): the agent kept the list in
    20	`localStorage.getItem("todo-list")` and reported that items "persist across page reloads and
    21	notebook reopenings". After an export and a reopen in a fresh browser context, the list was empty.
    22	
    23	## JSON state: `sticky` rewrites the cell's own source
    24	
    25	`@tomlarkworthy/sticky` wraps any view. The second argument is a literal slot; on every `input`
    26	event from the view, sticky writes `JSON.stringify(view.value)` into that slot in the cell's
    27	definition. Saving the notebook saves the source, so the value comes back on reopen.
    28	
    29	From `@tomlarkworthy/codestrates.doc` (lopebooks `tomlarkworthy_codestrates.html`), a whole HTML
    30	document kept this way:
    31	
    32	```js
    33	const <PID> = function _doc(sticky,codestrate,defaultCodestrate) {return (sticky(codestrate({ value: defaultCodestrate }), "<!doctype html>…"))};
    34	```
    35	
    36	Module source for a list, with the import (sticky is fetched from observablehq.com on first write
    37	and embedded in the file from then on):
    38	
    39	```js
    40	const _viewof_todos = function viewof_todos(sticky, todoList){return( sticky(todoList(), []) )};
    41	…
    42	  $def("_viewof_todos", "viewof todos", ["sticky", "todoList"], _viewof_todos);
    43	  $def("_todos", "todos", ["Generators", "viewof todos"], (G, v) => G.input(v));
    44	  main.define("module @tomlarkworthy/sticky", async () => runtime.module((await import("/@tomlarkworthy/sticky.js?v=4")).default));
    45	  main.define("sticky", ["module @tomlarkworthy/sticky", "@variable"], (_, v) => v.import("sticky", _));
    46	```
    47	
    48	The view must follow the Observable view contract, because sticky only talks to it through that.
    49	Sticky restores a saved value by **assigning `el.value` when the cell runs**, so the setter must
    50	re-render. A setter that only stores the value leaves the reopened list blank while the data is in
    51	the source. From `@tomlarkworthy/codestrates.codestratePlace` (lopebooks
    52	`tomlarkworthy_codestrates.html`, used as `sticky(codestratePlace($0))`):
    53	
    54	```js
    55	  Object.defineProperty(root, "value", {
    56	    get: () => state,
    57	    set: (v) => {
    58	      state = { where: v?.where === "webstrate" && v?.url ? "webstrate" : "notebook", url: v?.url || "" };
    59	      render();
    60	    }
    61	  });
    62	  render();
    63	  return root;
    64	```
    65	
    66	- `get` returns the state, JSON-serializable (arrays, objects, strings, numbers).
    67	- `set` replaces the state **and calls `render()`**.
    68	- after each user edit, `el.dispatchEvent(new Event("input", {bubbles: true}))`; sticky writes the
    69	  slot on that event.
    70	
    71	`Inputs.*` widgets already satisfy this: `sticky(Inputs.range([0, 100], {value: 50}), 50)`.
    72	
    73	One `sticky(` call per cell. Binary or large state (images, audio, datasets) goes in a file
    74	attachment instead (`how-file-attachments-work.md`).
    75	
    76	## Tell the user to save
    77	
    78	The state is in the page until the file is saved. After building it, say so: use Save in place (or
    79	export) before closing the tab.
    80	
    81	## Checking it
    82	
    83	`inspect_value` on the cell only shows the live value. Check both halves:
    84	
    85	1. Saving: drive the view (`eval_js`: set `.value`, dispatch `input`), then read `/notebook/<id>.js`;
    86	   the sticky slot must hold the new value.
    87	2. Reopening: set `.value` WITHOUT dispatching (what sticky does at boot) and confirm the element
    88	   now shows the items (`viewof_todos.textContent`).

    13	# Event handlers and buttons in cells: htl.html, not html; a button that acts on another cell's input; a download button; two inputs that update each other; a custom control (pad, canvas); limiting a number box to a range
    14	
    15	A cell that builds a clickable element and passes it a function (`onclick=${() => …}`) must build it
    16	with `htl.html`. The bare `html` built-in in a Lopecode notebook is the legacy stdlib template: it
    17	converts every interpolated value to a string, so the handler never becomes a listener.
    18	
    19	## What `html` does with a function
    20	
    21	Observed (robocoop-5, pomodoro prompt, 2026-09-27): the agent wrote
    22	
    23	```js
    24	const _toggleBtn = function toggleBtn(ru, mru, html){
    25	  return html`<button onclick=${() => { mru.value = !mru.value; }}>${ru ? '⏸ Pause' : '▶ Start'}</button>`;
    26	};
    27	```
    28	
    29	The arrow was stringified into the attribute; the `>` of `=>` ended the tag. The live button had
    30	attributes `onclick="()"` and `==""`, `typeof button.onclick` was `"object"` (null), and its text was
    31	`{ mru.value = !mru.value; }> ▶ Start`. Clicking it did nothing. The write still reported "all 18
    32	cells compute with no runtime error".
    33	
    34	## The form the corpus uses
    35	
    36	`htl.html` binds a function-valued `on…` attribute as an event listener. `@tomlarkworthy/gallery`
    37	`card` (lopebooks/notebooks/@tomlarkworthy_gallery.html) writes a mutable from a button this way:
    38	
    39	```js
    40	htl.html`<button class="card-star" onclick=${(e) => {
    41	  e.stopPropagation();
    42	  const current = new Map($edits.value);
    43	  …
    44	  $edits.value = current;
    45	}}>${featured ? "★" : "☆"}</button>`
    46	```
    47	
    48	`$edits` is that cell's name for its `"mutable edits"` input. The same shape in a module file, for a
    49	start/pause toggle:
    50	
    51	```js
    52	const _toggle = function toggle(htl, running, $running){return(
    53	  htl.html`<button onclick=${() => { $running.value = !running; }}>${running ? "Pause" : "Start"}</button>`
    54	)};
    55	// in define():
    56	$def("_toggle", "toggle", ["htl", "running", "mutable running"], _toggle);
    57	```
    58	
    59	`htl` is a built-in: list it as an input, as with `md` or `Inputs`. `@tomlarkworthy/lopecode-tour`
    60	`ui_prose` (lopecode/notebooks/@tomlarkworthy_lopecode-tour.html) has a smaller example:
    61	`htl.html\`<button onclick=${(e) => {e.target.innerHTML = "thanks"; e.stopPropagation()}}>click me!</button>\``.
    62	
    63	On 2026-09-27 an `on…=${…}` handler appeared inside `htl.html` in 247 notebook files (modules
    64	including `view`, `mermaid-lens`, `svg-lens`, `viewroutine`, `gallery`, `spreadsheet`,
    65	`lopecode-tour`). The bare-`html` form appeared in 16 files across 10 modules (`@endpointservices/login`,
    66	`animation`, `rate-estimation` and others), all written on observablehq.com, where `html` is htl. In
    67	Lopecode those handlers render as text too.

    69	## A button that acts on another cell's input
    70	
    71	The action runs once per click and reads the other input's value at click time. The cell holding the
    72	button lists the input's `viewof` and reads `.value` inside the click function.
    73	`@tomlarkworthy/editor-5` `up` (in 224 notebook files, e.g. lopebooks/notebooks/@tomlarkworthy_robocoop-5.html)
    74	reads `viewof editedCell` this way:
    75	
    76	```js
    77	const <PID> = function _up(Inputs,moveCell,$0){return(
    78	Inputs.button("⬆", {
    79	  reduce: () => moveCell($0.value, -1)
    80	})
    81	)};
    82	// in define():
    83	$def("<PID>", "viewof up", ["Inputs","moveCell","viewof editedCell"], <PID>);
    84	```
    85	
    86	The same `$0.value` read works inside an `htl.html` `onclick=${…}` function. When other cells show the
    87	result, `reduce` can return it (or a promise of it): the button's value cell then changes once per
    88	click, and cells that list it recompute once per click.
    89	
    90	Four forms that compile, report "all cells compute with no runtime error", and do not work. All four
    91	were written by robocoop-5 for "a text box and a button that summarises it" (20260928-0300-w19):
    92	
    93	- **The action cell lists the text's value cell** (`"inputText"`). It re-runs on every keystroke, so
    94	  the request is sent while the user types, and the button does nothing the text had not already done.
    95	- **A cell body that waits for a click** (`await new Promise(r => btn.addEventListener('click', r, {once: true}))`
    96	  in a `while (true)` loop). The cell's value never settles. In a replay of that module, text was typed,
    97	  the button clicked, and no request was sent.
    98	- **Finding the input through the DOM** (`btn.closest('.observablehq').querySelector('textarea')`,
    99	  `document.querySelector(…)`). Each cell renders into its own element, so the search from the
   100	  button's cell finds nothing; the handler read `''` and every click showed "Please paste some text first".
   101	- **Adding a listener to another cell's element from a cell that re-runs** (`summarizeButton.addEventListener('click', …)`
   102	  in a cell that also lists `model`). Each run adds one more listener and none is removed, so after the
   103	  model changed one click sent two requests, one with the old model.
   104	
   105	- **A click count that gates an action cell** (`viewof save = Inputs.button("Save")`, then a cell that
   106	  lists `save` and the form's value cells, `save > 0 && (() => { …; a.click(); })()`). After the
   107	  first click the count stays above 0, so the cell runs again whenever any listed value changes.
   108	  Observed (robocoop-5, a form with a download button, 20260928-0847-w10): after one click, editing
   109	  one text field twice offered two more downloads with no click.
   110	
   111	`Inputs.button` is the other working form when the button only needs to count clicks or emit a
   112	value; it is a `viewof` and follows the viewof page (`writing-cells-in-module-source.md`).

   114	## A button that downloads a file
   115	
   116	The cell's value is the button. The file is built and saved inside its click handler, so nothing is
   117	saved until it is clicked. The cell may list the values the file is made from; when they change the
   118	cell returns a new button and saves nothing. `@tomlarkworthy/suminagashi` `_download`
   119	(lopebooks/notebooks/@tomlarkworthy_suminagashi.html) saves a PNG this way. The same shape for a CSV:
   120	
   121	```js
   122	const _saveCsv = function saveCsv(htl, d3, rows){return(
   123	  htl.html`<button onclick=${() => {
   124	    const blob = new Blob([d3.csvFormat(rows)], {type: "text/csv"});
   125	    const link = htl.html`<a download="rows.csv" href=${URL.createObjectURL(blob)}>`;
   126	    link.click();
   127	    setTimeout(() => URL.revokeObjectURL(link.href), 1000);
   128	  }}>Download CSV</button>`
   129	)};
   130	// in define():
   131	$def("_saveCsv", "saveCsv", ["htl", "d3", "rows"], _saveCsv);
   132	```
   133	
   134	An async builder (a zip, a PDF) goes inside the handler: `onclick=${async () => { const blob = await build(rows); … }}`.
   135	The stdlib `DOM.download(blob, name, label)` returns a ready control too
   136	(`@tomlarkworthy/fileattachments` `_download_selected`, lopecode/notebooks/@tomlarkworthy_atlas.html);
   137	its first click builds the file and relabels the button "Download"; a second click saves it
   138	(`download.js` in the stdlib awaits the value before it sets `href`).

   140	## Listening on an Inputs view; two inputs that update each other
   141	
   142	An `Inputs.*` view (`Inputs.number`, `Inputs.text`, `Inputs.range`, …) is a `<form>` that wraps a
   143	label and the control. It is not the `<input>`. The view has `value` (read and write), and `input`
   144	events from the control bubble up to it. `document.activeElement` is never the view, because focus is
   145	on the `<input>` inside it, and the view has no `valueAsNumber`. The inner element is
   146	`view.querySelector("input")`.
   147	
   148	Observed (robocoop-5, temperature converter, 20260928-0510-w25): the agent guarded each listener with
   149	`document.activeElement === viewof_celsius` and read `viewof_celsius.valueAsNumber`. The guard was
   150	always false, so typing in either box changed nothing. The write reported "all 10 cells compute with
   151	no runtime error", and the agent told the user the converter worked. With the guard changed to
   152	`viewof_celsius.contains(document.activeElement)` and `.valueAsNumber` changed to `.value`, the same
   153	module passed.
   154	
   155	Two controls that show one quantity: keep the quantity in one hidden state cell,
   156	`viewof celsius = Inputs.input(20)`, and bind each control to it. `Inputs.bind(target, source)` copies
   157	`source.value` into the control, and on the control's `input` event writes the value back to the state
   158	and dispatches `input` on it, so the `celsius` value cell and every other bound control update. The
   159	corpus binds a second control to an existing view this way: `@tomlarkworthy/dataflow-templating` `_dtv2j`
   160	(lopecode/notebooks/@tomlarkworthy_atlas.html) is `Inputs.bind(Inputs.range([1, 4], { label: "widgets",
   161	step: 1 }), $0)` on `viewof widgetCount`. `Inputs.bind` copies values unchanged, so a control that
   162	shows a converted value needs a bind with a function each way:
   163	
   164	```js
   165	const _celsius = function celsius(Inputs){return( Inputs.input(20) )};
   166	const _bindVia = function bindVia(){return(
   167	(target, source, to, from, invalidation) => {
   168	  let fromTarget = false;
   169	  const onSource = () => { if (!fromTarget) target.value = to(source.value); };
   170	  const onTarget = () => {
   171	    if (!Number.isFinite(target.value)) return;
   172	    fromTarget = true;
   173	    source.value = from(target.value);
   174	    source.dispatchEvent(new Event("input", {bubbles: true}));
   175	    fromTarget = false;
   176	  };
   177	  onSource();
   178	  target.addEventListener("input", onTarget);
   179	  source.addEventListener("input", onSource);
   180	  invalidation?.then(() => source.removeEventListener("input", onSource));
   181	  return target;
   182	}
   183	)};
   184	const _cBox = function cBox(Inputs, $celsius, invalidation){return(
   185	  Inputs.bind(Inputs.number({label: "Celsius (°C)"}), $celsius, invalidation)
   186	)};
   187	const _fBox = function fBox(Inputs, bindVia, $celsius, invalidation){return(
   188	  bindVia(Inputs.number({label: "Fahrenheit (°F)"}), $celsius,
   189	    c => Math.round((c * 9 / 5 + 32) * 100) / 100, f => (f - 32) * 5 / 9, invalidation)
   190	)};
   191	// in define():
   192	$def("_celsius", "viewof celsius", ["Inputs"], _celsius);
   193	main.variable(observer("celsius")).define("celsius", ["Generators", "viewof celsius"], (G, _) => G.input(_));
   194	$def("_bindVia", "bindVia", [], _bindVia);
   195	$def("_cBox", "cBox", ["Inputs", "viewof celsius", "invalidation"], _cBox);
   196	$def("_fBox", "fBox", ["Inputs", "bindVia", "viewof celsius", "invalidation"], _fBox);
   197	```
   198	
   199	The control cells list `viewof celsius`, not `celsius`, so they are not rebuilt on each keystroke.
   200	Setting `.value` dispatches no event, so writes do not echo. `fromTarget` stops the state's `input`
   201	event from rewriting the box being typed in: without it, typing `98.60` in °F was reformatted to `98.6`
   202	under the cursor (probe `tools/scratch/rc5-sessions/s37-shared-state-bind.mjs`, 2026-09-28). With it,
   203	typing °F=212, °C=-40, °F=98.6 gave `celsius` 100, -40, 37, the other box 100, -40, 37, and the typed
   204	text kept each time.
   205	
   206	A listener cell that writes each box's converted value into the other box's `.value` also passes the
   207	converter eval, and this page recommended it until 2026-09-28. It leaves no single value to depend
   208	on: the `fahrenheit` value cell does not update when °C is typed, because setting `.value` dispatches
   209	nothing (follows from the no-echo behaviour above; not measured separately).
   210	
   211	## A custom control: set `.value`, then dispatch `input`
   212	
   213	A `viewof` cell can return any element: a pad, a canvas, an svg. The runtime reads the element's
   214	`.value` when the element dispatches `input`, so the value has to be set before the event:
   215	
   216	```js
   217	el.addEventListener("pointerdown", () => {
   218	  el.value = el.value + 1;                              // first
   219	  el.dispatchEvent(new Event("input", {bubbles: true})); // then
   220	});
   221	```
   222	
   223	Observed (robocoop-5 pairing, drum pad, 2026-09-28): the agent's pad dispatched `input` and then set
   224	`.value`, so each hit showed the previous hit's value. Every cell computed and the write reported no
   225	error. The user found it by playing the pad. `try_control` now presses a custom control with the
   226	pointer (down, up, click at its centre) when no `value` is given, and names this cause when the
   227	element's `.value` moved but the value cell did not. Probe `tools/scratch/rc5-sessions/s69-try-control-presses-custom-view.mjs`
   228	builds both orders: the lagging pad is flagged, the other reports `hits 0 → 1`.
   229	
   230	`setPointerCapture` inside a synthetic or already-released pointer event throws `NotFoundError`
   231	(seen in the same session, uncaught). Wrap it in `try`, or leave it out for a press that does not drag.
   232	
   233	## Limiting a number box: the range is the first argument
   234	
   235	`Inputs.number([min, max], options)` and `Inputs.range([min, max], options)` take the limits as the
   236	first argument. There is no `min` or `max` option: `Inputs.number({min: 0, max: 500})` ignores both
   237	without an error (`createRange` in `vendor/observable-inputs/src/range.js` destructures `extent:
   238	[min, max]` from the first argument and never reads `options.min`). `Inputs.range({min, max})`
   239	throws `object is not iterable`.
   240	
   241	Typed into the box the way a user does (probe `tools/scratch/rc5-train/20260928-0847/m31/inputs-behaviour.mjs`,
   242	2026-09-28, the Inputs shipped in robocoop-5):
   243	
   244	```
   245	typed   Inputs.number({min: 0, max: 500, value: 100})   Inputs.number([0, 500], {value: 100})
   246	-5      value -5, box valid                             value stays 100, box :invalid
   247	600     value 600, box valid                            value stays 100, box :invalid
   248	""      value unchanged, box :invalid                   value stays 100, box :invalid
   249	250     value 250                                       value 250
   250	```
   251	
   252	With the extent, an out-of-range, empty or non-numeric entry keeps the last good value and
   253	dispatches nothing, so dependent cells do not recompute; the box shows the entry the value does not
   254	have. A cell that should say what is wrong has to read the box itself
   255	(`viewof x.querySelector("input")`) or take `Inputs.text` and parse it.
   256	
   257	Observed (rc5-train m26, 2026-09-28, "make the AQI converter handle bad input"): in 3 of 3 runs the
   258	agent wrote `Inputs.number({ label: "AQI", value: 100, step: 1, min: 0, max: 500 })` and told the
   259	user the box now refuses values outside 0–500. It accepted -5 and 600.
   260	
   261	The corpus form, `@tomlarkworthy/inputs-reference._number_example`
   262	(lopebooks/notebooks/@tomlarkworthy_inputs-reference.html):
   263	
   264	```js
   265	Inputs.number([0, 10000], { label: 'price', value: 99, step: 0.01 })
   266	```
   267	
   268	A one-sided limit is `Inputs.number([0, Infinity], …)`: a non-finite or `null` end is no limit
   269	(`range.js`, `if (max == null || isNaN(max = +max)) max = Infinity`).

     7	# Keeping user state in the saved notebook file (localStorage does not travel)
     8	
     9	A Lopecode notebook is one HTML file. "It should still be there next time I open the notebook" means
    10	the state is written into that file when the notebook is saved (Save in place, or export), so it
    11	reopens with the file: in another browser, on another machine, or after the file is emailed.
    12	
    13	`localStorage`, `sessionStorage` and IndexedDB are none of these. They belong to one browser profile
    14	and one origin, are not part of the file, and throw on an opaque origin (a `blob:` fork). Use them
    15	only for per-browser settings that must *not* travel with the file: API keys, a model choice, a
    16	panel toggle. The corpus uses them for exactly that (`@tomlarkworthy/local-storage-view`, the
    17	robocoop-5 model picker and key field).
    18	
    19	Observed (run 20260927-2352-w6, todo-list prompt): the agent kept the list in
    20	`localStorage.getItem("todo-list")` and reported that items "persist across page reloads and
    21	notebook reopenings". After an export and a reopen in a fresh browser context, the list was empty.
    22	
    23	## JSON state: `sticky` rewrites the cell's own source
    24	
    25	`@tomlarkworthy/sticky` wraps any view. The second argument is a literal slot; on every `input`
    26	event from the view, sticky writes `JSON.stringify(view.value)` into that slot in the cell's
    27	definition. Saving the notebook saves the source, so the value comes back on reopen.
    28	
    29	From `@tomlarkworthy/codestrates.doc` (lopebooks `tomlarkworthy_codestrates.html`), a whole HTML
    30	document kept this way:
    31	
    32	```js
    33	const <PID> = function _doc(sticky,codestrate,defaultCodestrate) {return (sticky(codestrate({ value: defaultCodestrate }), "<!doctype html>…"))};
    34	```
    35	
    36	Module source for a list, with the import (sticky is fetched from observablehq.com on first write
    37	and embedded in the file from then on):
    38	
    39	```js
    40	const _viewof_todos = function viewof_todos(sticky, todoList){return( sticky(todoList(), []) )};
    41	…
    42	  $def("_viewof_todos", "viewof todos", ["sticky", "todoList"], _viewof_todos);
    43	  $def("_todos", "todos", ["Generators", "viewof todos"], (G, v) => G.input(v));
    44	  main.define("module @tomlarkworthy/sticky", async () => runtime.module((await import("/@tomlarkworthy/sticky.js?v=4")).default));
    45	  main.define("sticky", ["module @tomlarkworthy/sticky", "@variable"], (_, v) => v.import("sticky", _));
    46	```
    47	
    48	The view must follow the Observable view contract, because sticky only talks to it through that.
    49	Sticky restores a saved value by **assigning `el.value` when the cell runs**, so the setter must
    50	re-render. A setter that only stores the value leaves the reopened list blank while the data is in
    51	the source. From `@tomlarkworthy/codestrates.codestratePlace` (lopebooks
    52	`tomlarkworthy_codestrates.html`, used as `sticky(codestratePlace($0))`):
    53	
    54	```js

    13	# Event handlers and buttons in cells: htl.html, not html; a button that acts on another cell's input; a download button; two inputs that update each other; a custom control (pad, canvas); limiting a number box to a range
    14	
    15	A cell that builds a clickable element and passes it a function (`onclick=${() => …}`) must build it
    16	with `htl.html`. The bare `html` built-in in a Lopecode notebook is the legacy stdlib template: it
    17	converts every interpolated value to a string, so the handler never becomes a listener.
    18	
    19	## What `html` does with a function
    20	
    21	Observed (robocoop-5, pomodoro prompt, 2026-09-27): the agent wrote
    22	
    23	```js
    24	const _toggleBtn = function toggleBtn(ru, mru, html){
    25	  return html`<button onclick=${() => { mru.value = !mru.value; }}>${ru ? '⏸ Pause' : '▶ Start'}</button>`;
    26	};
    27	```
    28	
    29	The arrow was stringified into the attribute; the `>` of `=>` ended the tag. The live button had
    30	attributes `onclick="()"` and `==""`, `typeof button.onclick` was `"object"` (null), and its text was
    31	`{ mru.value = !mru.value; }> ▶ Start`. Clicking it did nothing. The write still reported "all 18
    32	cells compute with no runtime error".

    34	## The form the corpus uses
    35	
    36	`htl.html` binds a function-valued `on…` attribute as an event listener. `@tomlarkworthy/gallery`
    37	`card` (lopebooks/notebooks/@tomlarkworthy_gallery.html) writes a mutable from a button this way:
    38	
    39	```js
    40	htl.html`<button class="card-star" onclick=${(e) => {
    41	  e.stopPropagation();
    42	  const current = new Map($edits.value);
    43	  …
    44	  $edits.value = current;
    45	}}>${featured ? "★" : "☆"}</button>`
    46	```
    47	
    48	`$edits` is that cell's name for its `"mutable edits"` input. The same shape in a module file, for a
    49	start/pause toggle:
    50	
    51	```js
    52	const _toggle = function toggle(htl, running, $running){return(
    53	  htl.html`<button onclick=${() => { $running.value = !running; }}>${running ? "Pause" : "Start"}</button>`
    54	)};
    55	// in define():
    56	$def("_toggle", "toggle", ["htl", "running", "mutable running"], _toggle);
    57	```
    58	
    59	`htl` is a built-in: list it as an input, as with `md` or `Inputs`. `@tomlarkworthy/lopecode-tour`
    60	`ui_prose` (lopecode/notebooks/@tomlarkworthy_lopecode-tour.html) has a smaller example:
    61	`htl.html\`<button onclick=${(e) => {e.target.innerHTML = "thanks"; e.stopPropagation()}}>click me!</button>\``.
    62	
    63	On 2026-09-27 an `on…=${…}` handler appeared inside `htl.html` in 247 notebook files (modules
    64	including `view`, `mermaid-lens`, `svg-lens`, `viewroutine`, `gallery`, `spreadsheet`,
    65	`lopecode-tour`). The bare-`html` form appeared in 16 files across 10 modules (`@endpointservices/login`,
    66	`animation`, `rate-estimation` and others), all written on observablehq.com, where `html` is htl. In
    67	Lopecode those handlers render as text too.

    69	## A button that acts on another cell's input
    70	
    71	The action runs once per click and reads the other input's value at click time. The cell holding the
    72	button lists the input's `viewof` and reads `.value` inside the click function.
    73	`@tomlarkworthy/editor-5` `up` (in 224 notebook files, e.g. lopebooks/notebooks/@tomlarkworthy_robocoop-5.html)
    74	reads `viewof editedCell` this way:
    75	
    76	```js
    77	const <PID> = function _up(Inputs,moveCell,$0){return(
    78	Inputs.button("⬆", {
    79	  reduce: () => moveCell($0.value, -1)
    80	})
    81	)};
    82	// in define():
    83	$def("<PID>", "viewof up", ["Inputs","moveCell","viewof editedCell"], <PID>);
    84	```
    85	
    86	The same `$0.value` read works inside an `htl.html` `onclick=${…}` function. When other cells show the
    87	result, `reduce` can return it (or a promise of it): the button's value cell then changes once per
    88	click, and cells that list it recompute once per click.
    89	
    90	Four forms that compile, report "all cells compute with no runtime error", and do not work. All four
    91	were written by robocoop-5 for "a text box and a button that summarises it" (20260928-0300-w19):
    92	
    93	- **The action cell lists the text's value cell** (`"inputText"`). It re-runs on every keystroke, so
    94	  the request is sent while the user types, and the button does nothing the text had not already done.
    95	- **A cell body that waits for a click** (`await new Promise(r => btn.addEventListener('click', r, {once: true}))`
    96	  in a `while (true)` loop). The cell's value never settles. In a replay of that module, text was typed,
    97	  the button clicked, and no request was sent.
    98	- **Finding the input through the DOM** (`btn.closest('.observablehq').querySelector('textarea')`,
    99	  `document.querySelector(…)`). Each cell renders into its own element, so the search from the
   100	  button's cell finds nothing; the handler read `''` and every click showed "Please paste some text first".
   101	- **Adding a listener to another cell's element from a cell that re-runs** (`summarizeButton.addEventListener('click', …)`
   102	  in a cell that also lists `model`). Each run adds one more listener and none is removed, so after the
   103	  model changed one click sent two requests, one with the old model.
   104	
   105	- **A click count that gates an action cell** (`viewof save = Inputs.button("Save")`, then a cell that
   106	  lists `save` and the form's value cells, `save > 0 && (() => { …; a.click(); })()`). After the
   107	  first click the count stays above 0, so the cell runs again whenever any listed value changes.
   108	  Observed (robocoop-5, a form with a download button, 20260928-0847-w10): after one click, editing
   109	  one text field twice offered two more downloads with no click.

   111	`Inputs.button` is the other working form when the button only needs to count clicks or emit a
   112	value; it is a `viewof` and follows the viewof page (`writing-cells-in-module-source.md`).

   114	## A button that downloads a file
   115	
   116	The cell's value is the button. The file is built and saved inside its click handler, so nothing is
   117	saved until it is clicked. The cell may list the values the file is made from; when they change the
   118	cell returns a new button and saves nothing. `@tomlarkworthy/suminagashi` `_download`
   119	(lopebooks/notebooks/@tomlarkworthy_suminagashi.html) saves a PNG this way. The same shape for a CSV:
   120	
   121	```js
   122	const _saveCsv = function saveCsv(htl, d3, rows){return(
   123	  htl.html`<button onclick=${() => {
   124	    const blob = new Blob([d3.csvFormat(rows)], {type: "text/csv"});
   125	    const link = htl.html`<a download="rows.csv" href=${URL.createObjectURL(blob)}>`;
   126	    link.click();
   127	    setTimeout(() => URL.revokeObjectURL(link.href), 1000);
   128	  }}>Download CSV</button>`
   129	)};
   130	// in define():
   131	$def("_saveCsv", "saveCsv", ["htl", "d3", "rows"], _saveCsv);
   132	```
   133	
   134	An async builder (a zip, a PDF) goes inside the handler: `onclick=${async () => { const blob = await build(rows); … }}`.
   135	The stdlib `DOM.download(blob, name, label)` returns a ready control too
   136	(`@tomlarkworthy/fileattachments` `_download_selected`, lopecode/notebooks/@tomlarkworthy_atlas.html);
   137	its first click builds the file and relabels the button "Download"; a second click saves it
   138	(`download.js` in the stdlib awaits the value before it sets `href`).

   140	## Listening on an Inputs view; two inputs that update each other
   141	
   142	An `Inputs.*` view (`Inputs.number`, `Inputs.text`, `Inputs.range`, …) is a `<form>` that wraps a
   143	label and the control. It is not the `<input>`. The view has `value` (read and write), and `input`
   144	events from the control bubble up to it. `document.activeElement` is never the view, because focus is
   145	on the `<input>` inside it, and the view has no `valueAsNumber`. The inner element is
   146	`view.querySelector("input")`.
   147	
   148	Observed (robocoop-5, temperature converter, 20260928-0510-w25): the agent guarded each listener with
   149	`document.activeElement === viewof_celsius` and read `viewof_celsius.valueAsNumber`. The guard was
   150	always false, so typing in either box changed nothing. The write reported "all 10 cells compute with
   151	no runtime error", and the agent told the user the converter worked. With the guard changed to
   152	`viewof_celsius.contains(document.activeElement)` and `.valueAsNumber` changed to `.value`, the same
   153	module passed.
   154	
   155	Two controls that show one quantity: keep the quantity in one hidden state cell,
   156	`viewof celsius = Inputs.input(20)`, and bind each control to it. `Inputs.bind(target, source)` copies
   157	`source.value` into the control, and on the control's `input` event writes the value back to the state
   158	and dispatches `input` on it, so the `celsius` value cell and every other bound control update. The
   159	corpus binds a second control to an existing view this way: `@tomlarkworthy/dataflow-templating` `_dtv2j`
   160	(lopecode/notebooks/@tomlarkworthy_atlas.html) is `Inputs.bind(Inputs.range([1, 4], { label: "widgets",
   161	step: 1 }), $0)` on `viewof widgetCount`. `Inputs.bind` copies values unchanged, so a control that
   162	shows a converted value needs a bind with a function each way:
   163	
   164	```js
   165	const _celsius = function celsius(Inputs){return( Inputs.input(20) )};
   166	const _bindVia = function bindVia(){return(
   167	(target, source, to, from, invalidation) => {
   168	  let fromTarget = false;
   169	  const onSource = () => { if (!fromTarget) target.value = to(source.value); };
   170	  const onTarget = () => {
   171	    if (!Number.isFinite(target.value)) return;
   172	    fromTarget = true;
   173	    source.value = from(target.value);
   174	    source.dispatchEvent(new Event("input", {bubbles: true}));
   175	    fromTarget = false;
   176	  };
   177	  onSource();
   178	  target.addEventListener("input", onTarget);
   179	  source.addEventListener("input", onSource);
   180	  invalidation?.then(() => source.removeEventListener("input", onSource));
   181	  return target;
   182	}
   183	)};
   184	const _cBox = function cBox(Inputs, $celsius, invalidation){return(
   185	  Inputs.bind(Inputs.number({label: "Celsius (°C)"}), $celsius, invalidation)
   186	)};
   187	const _fBox = function fBox(Inputs, bindVia, $celsius, invalidation){return(
   188	  bindVia(Inputs.number({label: "Fahrenheit (°F)"}), $celsius,
   189	    c => Math.round((c * 9 / 5 + 32) * 100) / 100, f => (f - 32) * 5 / 9, invalidation)
   190	)};
   191	// in define():
   192	$def("_celsius", "viewof celsius", ["Inputs"], _celsius);
   193	main.variable(observer("celsius")).define("celsius", ["Generators", "viewof celsius"], (G, _) => G.input(_));
   194	$def("_bindVia", "bindVia", [], _bindVia);
   195	$def("_cBox", "cBox", ["Inputs", "viewof celsius", "invalidation"], _cBox);
   196	$def("_fBox", "fBox", ["Inputs", "bindVia", "viewof celsius", "invalidation"], _fBox);
   197	```
   198	
   199	The control cells list `viewof celsius`, not `celsius`, so they are not rebuilt on each keystroke.
   200	Setting `.value` dispatches no event, so writes do not echo. `fromTarget` stops the state's `input`
   201	event from rewriting the box being typed in: without it, typing `98.60` in °F was reformatted to `98.6`
   202	under the cursor (probe `tools/scratch/rc5-sessions/s37-shared-state-bind.mjs`, 2026-09-28). With it,
   203	typing °F=212, °C=-40, °F=98.6 gave `celsius` 100, -40, 37, the other box 100, -40, 37, and the typed
   204	text kept each time.
   205	
   206	A listener cell that writes each box's converted value into the other box's `.value` also passes the
   207	converter eval, and this page recommended it until 2026-09-28. It leaves no single value to depend
   208	on: the `fahrenheit` value cell does not update when °C is typed, because setting `.value` dispatches
   209	nothing (follows from the no-echo behaviour above; not measured separately).
   210	
   211	## A custom control: set `.value`, then dispatch `input`
   212	
   213	A `viewof` cell can return any element: a pad, a canvas, an svg. The runtime reads the element's
   214	`.value` when the element dispatches `input`, so the value has to be set before the event:
   215	
   216	```js
   217	el.addEventListener("pointerdown", () => {
   218	  el.value = el.value + 1;                              // first
   219	  el.dispatchEvent(new Event("input", {bubbles: true})); // then
   220	});
   221	```
   222	
   223	Observed (robocoop-5 pairing, drum pad, 2026-09-28): the agent's pad dispatched `input` and then set
   224	`.value`, so each hit showed the previous hit's value. Every cell computed and the write reported no
   225	error. The user found it by playing the pad. `try_control` now presses a custom control with the
   226	pointer (down, up, click at its centre) when no `value` is given, and names this cause when the
   227	element's `.value` moved but the value cell did not. Probe `tools/scratch/rc5-sessions/s69-try-control-presses-custom-view.mjs`
   228	builds both orders: the lagging pad is flagged, the other reports `hits 0 → 1`.
   229	
   230	`setPointerCapture` inside a synthetic or already-released pointer event throws `NotFoundError`
   231	(seen in the same session, uncaught). Wrap it in `try`, or leave it out for a press that does not drag.
   232	
   233	## Limiting a number box: the range is the first argument
   234	
   235	`Inputs.number([min, max], options)` and `Inputs.range([min, max], options)` take the limits as the
   236	first argument. There is no `min` or `max` option: `Inputs.number({min: 0, max: 500})` ignores both
   237	without an error (`createRange` in `vendor/observable-inputs/src/range.js` destructures `extent:
   238	[min, max]` from the first argument and never reads `options.min`). `Inputs.range({min, max})`
   239	throws `object is not iterable`.
   240	
   241	Typed into the box the way a user does (probe `tools/scratch/rc5-train/20260928-0847/m31/inputs-behaviour.mjs`,
   242	2026-09-28, the Inputs shipped in robocoop-5):
   243	
   244	```
   245	typed   Inputs.number({min: 0, max: 500, value: 100})   Inputs.number([0, 500], {value: 100})
   246	-5      value -5, box valid                             value stays 100, box :invalid
   247	600     value 600, box valid                            value stays 100, box :invalid
   248	""      value unchanged, box :invalid                   value stays 100, box :invalid
   249	250     value 250                                       value 250
   250	```
   251	
   252	With the extent, an out-of-range, empty or non-numeric entry keeps the last good value and
   253	dispatches nothing, so dependent cells do not recompute; the box shows the entry the value does not
   254	have. A cell that should say what is wrong has to read the box itself
   255	(`viewof x.querySelector("input")`) or take `Inputs.text` and parse it.
   256	
   257	Observed (rc5-train m26, 2026-09-28, "make the AQI converter handle bad input"): in 3 of 3 runs the
   258	agent wrote `Inputs.number({ label: "AQI", value: 100, step: 1, min: 0, max: 500 })` and told the
   259	user the box now refuses values outside 0–500. It accepted -5 and 600.
   260	
   261	The corpus form, `@tomlarkworthy/inputs-reference._number_example`
   262	(lopebooks/notebooks/@tomlarkworthy_inputs-reference.html):
   263	
   264	```js
   265	Inputs.number([0, 10000], { label: 'price', value: 99, step: 0.01 })
   266	```
   267	
   268	A one-sided limit is `Inputs.number([0, Infinity], …)`: a non-finite or `null` end is no limit
   269	(`range.js`, `if (max == null || isNaN(max = +max)) max = Infinity`).

    43	## How the imports work
    44	
    45	Two forms. Both go at the bottom of `define()`, one binding line per imported name. A write containing these
    46	lines is refused until `writing-cells-in-module-source.md` has been read; read it before the first write.
    47	
    48	**From an atproto blob.** `getBlob?cid=…` is the module's source, addressed by its content hash,
    49	so it is pinned to one version. The `"@ns/name" &&` before `runtime.module` is required: the URL
    50	does not spell the module's name, and the exporter reads the name from that string. Without it, a
    51	save wrote the module as `<unknown 0.59…>` (probe `s38-atproto-blob-import.mjs`).

    54	main.define("module @tomlarkworthy/sheet", async () => "@tomlarkworthy/sheet" && runtime.module((await import("https://earthstar.us-east.host.bsky.network/xrpc/com.atproto.sync.getBlob?did=did:plc:j7nm3lrd5h7fm3sfhcv3lhfv&cid=bafkreictiyvkeezqxxbuvqd74f6qzkglc3vsgume6fz5gz5bgph2vq4vga")).default));
    55	main.define("sheet", ["module @tomlarkworthy/sheet", "@variable"], (_, v) => v.import("sheet", _));
    56	```

    58	**From observablehq.com**, for a module not on the PDS. If the page already embeds the module,
    59	this resolves to the embedded copy.

   317	A Word `.docx` (or Excel `.xlsx`) file is a zip of XML parts. `JSZip` from
   318	`@tomlarkworthy/jszip-3-10-1` is embedded in robocoop-5, so a save keeps it; the corpus zips files with
   319	it in `@tomlarkworthy/local-change-history` `_exportFsToZip` (lopecode/notebooks/@tomlarkworthy_exporter-3.html:
   320	`new JSZip()`, `zip.file(path, data)`, `zip.generateAsync({type: "blob"})`). Three parts make a
   321	document with one paragraph per string:

   323	```js
   324	$def("_docxBlob", "docxBlob", ["JSZip"], (JSZip) => async (paragraphs) => {
   325	  const esc = s => String(s).replace(/&/g, "&").replace(/</g, "<").replace(/>/g, ">");
   326	  const zip = new JSZip();
   327	  zip.file("[Content_Types].xml", '<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8" standalone="yes"?><Types xmlns="http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/package/2006/content-types"><Default Extension="rels" ContentType="application/vnd.openxmlformats-package.relationships+xml"/><Default Extension="xml" ContentType="application/xml"/><Override PartName="/word/document.xml" ContentType="application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document.main+xml"/></Types>');

   329	  const body = paragraphs.map(p => '<w:p><w:r><w:t xml:space="preserve">' + esc(p) + '</w:t></w:r></w:p>').join("");
   330	  zip.file("word/document.xml", '<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8" standalone="yes"?><w:document xmlns:w="http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/wordprocessingml/2006/main"><w:body>' + body + '</w:body></w:document>');
   331	  return zip.generateAsync({type: "blob", mimeType: "application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document"});
   332	});
   333	$def("_saveDocx", "saveDocx", ["htl", "docxBlob", "notes"], (htl, docxBlob, notes) =>
   334	  htl.html`<button onclick=${async () => {
   335	    const link = htl.html`<a download="notes.docx" href=${URL.createObjectURL(await docxBlob(notes.split("\n")))}>`;
   336	    link.click();
   337	  }}>Download Word document</button>`);
   338	main.define("module @tomlarkworthy/jszip-3-10-1", async () => runtime.module((await import("/@tomlarkworthy/jszip-3-10-1.js?v=4")).default));

   340	```
   341	
   342	An `.xlsx` is the same zip with five parts. `rows` is an array of arrays, the first the header; a
   343	number cell is `<c><v>` and a text cell is an inline string, so no sharedStrings part is needed:
   344	
   345	```js
   346	$def("_xlsxBlob", "xlsxBlob", ["JSZip"], (JSZip) => async (rows) => {
   347	  const esc = s => String(s).replace(/&/g, "&").replace(/</g, "<").replace(/>/g, ">");
   348	  const cell = v => typeof v === "number" ? "<c><v>" + v + "</v></c>" : '<c t="inlineStr"><is><t>' + esc(v) + "</t></is></c>";
   349	  const R = "http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/", X = '<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8" standalone="yes"?>';
   350	  const zip = new JSZip();
   351	  zip.file("[Content_Types].xml", X + '<Types xmlns="' + R + 'package/2006/content-types"><Default Extension="rels" ContentType="application/vnd.openxmlformats-package.relationships+xml"/><Default Extension="xml" ContentType="application/xml"/><Override PartName="/xl/workbook.xml" ContentType="application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet.main+xml"/><Override PartName="/xl/worksheets/sheet1.xml" ContentType="application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.worksheet+xml"/></Types>');
   352	  zip.file("_rels/.rels", X + '<Relationships xmlns="' + R + 'package/2006/relationships"><Relationship Id="rId1" Type="' + R + 'officeDocument/2006/relationships/officeDocument" Target="xl/workbook.xml"/></Relationships>');

   381	## sign-a-pdf
   382	
   383	Its `pdfLib` (pdf-lib, which creates and edits PDFs) and `pdfjs` (PDF.js 2.10.12, which renders
   384	pages) are stored in the notebook as file attachments. Not on the PDS.
   385	
   386	```js
   387	main.define("module @tomlarkworthy/sign-a-pdf", async () => runtime.module((await import("/@tomlarkworthy/sign-a-pdf.js?v=4")).default));
   388	main.define("pdfLib", ["module @tomlarkworthy/sign-a-pdf", "@variable"], (_, v) => v.import("pdfLib", _));
   389	const _pdfBytes = async function pdfBytes(pdfLib){
   390	  const doc = await pdfLib.PDFDocument.create();
   391	  const page = doc.addPage([400, 200]);
   392	  const font = await doc.embedFont(pdfLib.StandardFonts.Helvetica);
   393	  page.drawText("Hello from a cell", {x: 40, y: 100, size: 24, font});
   394	  return doc.save();                       // Uint8Array
   395	};
   396	$def("_pdfBytes", "pdfBytes", ["pdfLib"], _pdfBytes);
   397	$def("_pdfLink", "pdfLink", ["pdfBytes", "htl"], (pdfBytes, htl) => {
   398	  const blob = new Blob([pdfBytes], {type: "application/pdf"});
   399	  return htl.html`<a href=${URL.createObjectURL(blob)} download="hello.pdf">Download PDF (${blob.size} bytes)</a>`;
   400	});
   401	```
   402	
   403	A font belongs to the `PDFDocument` that embedded it. Embed it in the same cell that creates and
   404	saves that document, as `pdfBytes` above does; `@tomlarkworthy/sign-a-pdf` `_embed` likewise embeds
   405	its image into the `pdfDoc` that `_url` saves. A font taken from another document, such as a separate
   406	`font = otherDoc.embedFont(...)` cell, draws without an error, but the saved file refers to an object
   407	that is not a font. In run 20260928-0847-w16 every line drawn in the bold font (the title, the
   408	headings and the total row) was missing when the PDF was opened, while the cells reported no error.
   409	
   410	Importing either name adds about 3.4 MB of attachments to every save. To load an existing file,
   411	use `pdfLib.PDFDocument.load(await file.arrayBuffer())`. `pdfjs` rendering failed in a saved
   412	notebook opened from `file://` (`Setting up fake worker failed`), and worked when the same file
   413	was served over http. Pass `bytes.slice()` to `pdfjs.getDocument`, because it takes ownership of
   414	the buffer.

    43	## How the imports work
    44	
    45	Two forms. Both go at the bottom of `define()`, one binding line per imported name. A write containing these
    46	lines is refused until `writing-cells-in-module-source.md` has been read; read it before the first write.
    47	
    48	**From an atproto blob.** `getBlob?cid=…` is the module's source, addressed by its content hash,
    49	so it is pinned to one version. The `"@ns/name" &&` before `runtime.module` is required: the URL
    50	does not spell the module's name, and the exporter reads the name from that string. Without it, a
    51	save wrote the module as `<unknown 0.59…>` (probe `s38-atproto-blob-import.mjs`).
    52	
    53	```js
    54	main.define("module @tomlarkworthy/sheet", async () => "@tomlarkworthy/sheet" && runtime.module((await import("https://earthstar.us-east.host.bsky.network/xrpc/com.atproto.sync.getBlob?did=did:plc:j7nm3lrd5h7fm3sfhcv3lhfv&cid=bafkreictiyvkeezqxxbuvqd74f6qzkglc3vsgume6fz5gz5bgph2vq4vga")).default));
    55	main.define("sheet", ["module @tomlarkworthy/sheet", "@variable"], (_, v) => v.import("sheet", _));
    56	```

    58	**From observablehq.com**, for a module not on the PDS. If the page already embeds the module,
    59	this resolves to the embedded copy.

    61	```js
    62	main.define("module @tomlarkworthy/slides", async () => runtime.module((await import("/@tomlarkworthy/slides.js?v=4")).default));
    63	```

    66	embeds them. In every example below, the saved file then worked with the network off, except

   381	## sign-a-pdf
   382	
   383	Its `pdfLib` (pdf-lib, which creates and edits PDFs) and `pdfjs` (PDF.js 2.10.12, which renders
   384	pages) are stored in the notebook as file attachments. Not on the PDS.
   385	
   386	```js
   387	main.define("module @tomlarkworthy/sign-a-pdf", async () => runtime.module((await import("/@tomlarkworthy/sign-a-pdf.js?v=4")).default));
   388	main.define("pdfLib", ["module @tomlarkworthy/sign-a-pdf", "@variable"], (_, v) => v.import("pdfLib", _));
   389	const _pdfBytes = async function pdfBytes(pdfLib){
   390	  const doc = await pdfLib.PDFDocument.create();
   391	  const page = doc.addPage([400, 200]);
   392	  const font = await doc.embedFont(pdfLib.StandardFonts.Helvetica);
   393	  page.drawText("Hello from a cell", {x: 40, y: 100, size: 24, font});
   394	  return doc.save();                       // Uint8Array
   395	};
   396	$def("_pdfBytes", "pdfBytes", ["pdfLib"], _pdfBytes);
   397	$def("_pdfLink", "pdfLink", ["pdfBytes", "htl"], (pdfBytes, htl) => {
   398	  const blob = new Blob([pdfBytes], {type: "application/pdf"});
   399	  return htl.html`<a href=${URL.createObjectURL(blob)} download="hello.pdf">Download PDF (${blob.size} bytes)</a>`;
   400	});
   401	```
   402	
   403	A font belongs to the `PDFDocument` that embedded it. Embed it in the same cell that creates and
   404	saves that document, as `pdfBytes` above does; `@tomlarkworthy/sign-a-pdf` `_embed` likewise embeds
   405	its image into the `pdfDoc` that `_url` saves. A font taken from another document, such as a separate
   406	`font = otherDoc.embedFont(...)` cell, draws without an error, but the saved file refers to an object
   407	that is not a font. In run 20260928-0847-w16 every line drawn in the bold font (the title, the
   408	headings and the total row) was missing when the PDF was opened, while the cells reported no error.
   409	
   410	Importing either name adds about 3.4 MB of attachments to every save. To load an existing file,
   411	use `pdfLib.PDFDocument.load(await file.arrayBuffer())`. `pdfjs` rendering failed in a saved
   412	notebook opened from `file://` (`Setting up fake worker failed`), and worked when the same file
   413	was served over http. Pass `bytes.slice()` to `pdfjs.getDocument`, because it takes ownership of
   414	the buffer.

    43	## How the imports work
    44	
    45	Two forms. Both go at the bottom of `define()`, one binding line per imported name. A write containing these
    46	lines is refused until `writing-cells-in-module-source.md` has been read; read it before the first write.
    47	
    48	**From an atproto blob.** `getBlob?cid=…` is the module's source, addressed by its content hash,
    49	so it is pinned to one version. The `"@ns/name" &&` before `runtime.module` is required: the URL
    50	does not spell the module's name, and the exporter reads the name from that string. Without it, a
    51	save wrote the module as `<unknown 0.59…>` (probe `s38-atproto-blob-import.mjs`).
    52	
    53	```js
    54	main.define("module @tomlarkworthy/sheet", async () => "@tomlarkworthy/sheet" && runtime.module((await import("https://earthstar.us-east.host.bsky.network/xrpc/com.atproto.sync.getBlob?did=did:plc:j7nm3lrd5h7fm3sfhcv3lhfv&cid=bafkreictiyvkeezqxxbuvqd74f6qzkglc3vsgume6fz5gz5bgph2vq4vga")).default));
    55	main.define("sheet", ["module @tomlarkworthy/sheet", "@variable"], (_, v) => v.import("sheet", _));
    56	```
    57	
    58	**From observablehq.com**, for a module not on the PDS. If the page already embeds the module,
    59	this resolves to the embedded copy.
    60	
    61	```js
    62	main.define("module @tomlarkworthy/slides", async () => runtime.module((await import("/@tomlarkworthy/slides.js?v=4")).default));
    63	```
    64	
    65	Either way the module and its own imports are fetched when the write applies, and the next save
    66	embeds them. In every example below, the saved file then worked with the network off, except
    67	where a section says otherwise.
    68	
    69	Several modules take `module:` (sheet, slides, grid-container, parametric-svg). They need the
    70	Module value. `thisModule()` from `@tomlarkworthy/runtime-sdk` returns a view of it, so read it

   167	## local-storage-view
   168	
   169	A view whose value is `localStorage[key]`: kept per browser across reloads, not in the file.
   170	Embedded in the robocoop-5 notebook, so the Observable-path form works offline too.
   171	
   172	```js
   173	main.define("module @tomlarkworthy/local-storage-view", async () => runtime.module((await import("/@tomlarkworthy/local-storage-view.js?v=4")).default));

   176	  Inputs.bind(Inputs.range([0, 100], {label: "volume", step: 1, value: 10}), localStorageView("demo-volume", {defaultValue: 10})));

   181	new key reads `null`, and `Inputs.bind` then sets a range to its minimum. Values are strings
   182	unless `json: true`, and a stored `0` or `""` reads as the default. For an object, use
   183	`{json: true}` with no default and handle `null`: an object `defaultValue` renders a collapsed
   184	inspector, which made `write_file` hang in this harness until `summarizejs` was fixed on

   259	The stdlib `mermaid` tag renders mermaid syntax to an `<svg>`. It needs no import line: list
   260	`"mermaid"` as a dependency.

   263	$def("_diagram", "diagram", ["mermaid"], (mermaid) => mermaid`graph TD

   275	`${…}` hole form is `@tomlarkworthy/mermaid-lens._holeDemo`). Wrapping the textarea in `sticky`

   277	saved file reopens with the edited text. A reload without saving loses the edits either way.

   304	A `<canvas>` saved as PNG keeps a transparent background wherever nothing was drawn, even though it
   305	looks white on the page. Fill the background before drawing, and after each clear. In 4 of 7
   306	agent-built sketch pads (rc5-train w3, 2026-09-28), the downloaded PNG was transparent. The corpus
   307	pattern (`@tomlarkworthy/suminagashi` `_download`) builds the file when the button is clicked, so it
   308	holds the current drawing:
   309	
   310	```js
   311	htl.html`<button onclick=${() => canvas.toBlob(blob => {
   312	  const link = htl.html`<a download="drawing.png" href=${URL.createObjectURL(blob)}>`;
   313	  link.click();
   314	}, "image/png")}>Download PNG</button>`
   315	``` For a PDF that works offline, use `pdfLib` (next section).

    43	## How the imports work
    44	
    45	Two forms. Both go at the bottom of `define()`, one binding line per imported name. A write containing these
    46	lines is refused until `writing-cells-in-module-source.md` has been read; read it before the first write.
    47	
    48	**From an atproto blob.** `getBlob?cid=…` is the module's source, addressed by its content hash,
    49	so it is pinned to one version. The `"@ns/name" &&` before `runtime.module` is required: the URL
    50	does not spell the module's name, and the exporter reads the name from that string. Without it, a
    51	save wrote the module as `<unknown 0.59…>` (probe `s38-atproto-blob-import.mjs`).
    52	
    53	```js
    54	main.define("module @tomlarkworthy/sheet", async () => "@tomlarkworthy/sheet" && runtime.module((await import("https://earthstar.us-east.host.bsky.network/xrpc/com.atproto.sync.getBlob?did=did:plc:j7nm3lrd5h7fm3sfhcv3lhfv&cid=bafkreictiyvkeezqxxbuvqd74f6qzkglc3vsgume6fz5gz5bgph2vq4vga")).default));
    55	main.define("sheet", ["module @tomlarkworthy/sheet", "@variable"], (_, v) => v.import("sheet", _));
    56	```
    57	
    58	**From observablehq.com**, for a module not on the PDS. If the page already embeds the module,
    59	this resolves to the embedded copy.
    60	
    61	```js
    62	main.define("module @tomlarkworthy/slides", async () => runtime.module((await import("/@tomlarkworthy/slides.js?v=4")).default));
    63	```
    64	
    65	Either way the module and its own imports are fetched when the write applies, and the next save
    66	embeds them. In every example below, the saved file then worked with the network off, except
    67	where a section says otherwise.

    70	Module value. `thisModule()` from `@tomlarkworthy/runtime-sdk` returns a view of it, so read it

   318	`@tomlarkworthy/jszip-3-10-1` is embedded in robocoop-5, so a save keeps it; the corpus zips files with

   327	  zip.file("[Content_Types].xml", '<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8" standalone="yes"?><Types xmlns="http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/package/2006/content-types"><Default Extension="rels" ContentType="application/vnd.openxmlformats-package.relationships+xml"/><Default Extension="xml" ContentType="application/xml"/><Override PartName="/word/document.xml" ContentType="application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document.main+xml"/></Types>');

   382	
   383	Its `pdfLib` (pdf-lib, which creates and edits PDFs) and `pdfjs` (PDF.js 2.10.12, which renders
   384	pages) are stored in the notebook as file attachments. Not on the PDS.
   385	
   386	```js
   387	main.define("module @tomlarkworthy/sign-a-pdf", async () => runtime.module((await import("/@tomlarkworthy/sign-a-pdf.js?v=4")).default));
   388	main.define("pdfLib", ["module @tomlarkworthy/sign-a-pdf", "@variable"], (_, v) => v.import("pdfLib", _));
   389	const _pdfBytes = async function pdfBytes(pdfLib){
   390	  const doc = await pdfLib.PDFDocument.create();
   391	  const page = doc.addPage([400, 200]);
   392	  const font = await doc.embedFont(pdfLib.StandardFonts.Helvetica);
   393	  page.drawText("Hello from a cell", {x: 40, y: 100, size: 24, font});
   394	  return doc.save();                       // Uint8Array
   395	};
   396	$def("_pdfBytes", "pdfBytes", ["pdfLib"], _pdfBytes);
   397	$def("_pdfLink", "pdfLink", ["pdfBytes", "htl"], (pdfBytes, htl) => {
   398	  const blob = new Blob([pdfBytes], {type: "application/pdf"});
   399	  return htl.html`<a href=${URL.createObjectURL(blob)} download="hello.pdf">Download PDF (${blob.size} bytes)</a>`;
   400	});
   401	```
   402	
   403	A font belongs to the `PDFDocument` that embedded it. Embed it in the same cell that creates and
   404	saves that document, as `pdfBytes` above does; `@tomlarkworthy/sign-a-pdf` `_embed` likewise embeds
   405	its image into the `pdfDoc` that `_url` saves. A font taken from another document, such as a separate
   406	`font = otherDoc.embedFont(...)` cell, draws without an error, but the saved file refers to an object
   407	that is not a font. In run 20260928-0847-w16 every line drawn in the bold font (the title, the
   408	headings and the total row) was missing when the PDF was opened, while the cells reported no error.
   409	
   410	Importing either name adds about 3.4 MB of attachments to every save. To load an existing file,
   411	use `pdfLib.PDFDocument.load(await file.arrayBuffer())`. `pdfjs` rendering failed in a saved
   412	notebook opened from `file://` (`Setting up fake worker failed`), and worked when the same file
   413	was served over http. Pass `bytes.slice()` to `pdfjs.getDocument`, because it takes ownership of
   414	the buffer.

    43	## How the imports work
    44	
    45	Two forms. Both go at the bottom of `define()`, one binding line per imported name. A write containing these
    46	lines is refused until `writing-cells-in-module-source.md` has been read; read it before the first write.
    47	
    48	**From an atproto blob.** `getBlob?cid=…` is the module's source, addressed by its content hash,
    49	so it is pinned to one version. The `"@ns/name" &&` before `runtime.module` is required: the URL
    50	does not spell the module's name, and the exporter reads the name from that string. Without it, a
    51	save wrote the module as `<unknown 0.59…>` (probe `s38-atproto-blob-import.mjs`).
    52	
    53	```js
    54	main.define("module @tomlarkworthy/sheet", async () => "@tomlarkworthy/sheet" && runtime.module((await import("https://earthstar.us-east.host.bsky.network/xrpc/com.atproto.sync.getBlob?did=did:plc:j7nm3lrd5h7fm3sfhcv3lhfv&cid=bafkreictiyvkeezqxxbuvqd74f6qzkglc3vsgume6fz5gz5bgph2vq4vga")).default));
    55	main.define("sheet", ["module @tomlarkworthy/sheet", "@variable"], (_, v) => v.import("sheet", _));
    56	```
    57	
    58	**From observablehq.com**, for a module not on the PDS. If the page already embeds the module,
    59	this resolves to the embedded copy.
    60	
    61	```js
    62	main.define("module @tomlarkworthy/slides", async () => runtime.module((await import("/@tomlarkworthy/slides.js?v=4")).default));
    63	```
    64	
    65	Either way the module and its own imports are fetched when the write applies, and the next save
    66	embeds them. In every example below, the saved file then worked with the network off, except
    67	where a section says otherwise.
    68	
    69	Several modules take `module:` (sheet, slides, grid-container, parametric-svg). They need the
    70	Module value. `thisModule()` from `@tomlarkworthy/runtime-sdk` returns a view of it, so read it
    71	through a `viewof` + `Generators.input` pair. Passing `thisModule()` directly failed with
    72	`Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'get')`. grid-container's default `module` is not
    73	your module.

    81	$def("_my", "myModule", ["Generators", "viewof myModule"], (G, v) => G.input(v));
